#1706. Arsenal maintain perfect start but lack firepower of rivals

Bukayo Saka maintained Arsenal’s perfect start to the season, but Mikel Arteta appeared to acknowledge that the Premier League champions are in danger of leaving themselves short in attack.

There is still time for Arteta to add another forward to his squad and whether he does so or not could be important, with the transfer window closing on Tuesday night.

Having sold Leandro Trossard and with Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus on the verge of moves away, Arsenal appear light of forward options.

Lyon winger Malick Fofana has been offered to the club, but he is an underwhelming target given Morgan Rogers and Vinícius Júnior were pursued earlier in the summer.

“We are trying to improve the squad,” Arteta, the Arsenal head coach, said. “Until Tuesday night, we’re going to try to do that. I’ve been disconnected from the world for 24 hours because I think my energy and focus has to be on the match. I will give it [my energy] now.”

Asked if he currently has enough depth in forward positions, Arteta added: “It depends if everybody is fit or not. We know that the depth has to be really big when you are fighting for four competitions. So we’re going to try to do that.”

This was an Aston Villa team there for the taking after being gutted by their Premier League rivals and still waiting for new signings to be ready to play and gel.

But Arsenal made hard work of their victory and one senses there will be more games like this if Arteta has to rely on what he has already got until at least January.

Chelsea are showing they can score goals for fun having spent £117m on Rogers. Manchester City are strengthening their firepower with the signing of Iliman Ndiaye and Bradley Barcola has joined Liverpool. Arsenal have the defence and the midfield, but not necessarily the depth of quality in forward positions of their rivals.

0.52 - Arsenal faced the fewest shots (11), the fewest shots on target (1) and allowed their opponents the lowest xG (0.52) across the first two matchdays of the Premier League season.🔒 Locked. pic.twitter.com/blSUAeqoLb

Christos Tzolis is the lone attacking signing to date and there was evidence at Villa Park that it will be a risk to rely too heavily on the Greek winger.

Tzolis had made an exciting start to his Arsenal career in the Community Shield and the first Premier League victory over Coventry City, but he had to be taken off at half-time on Monday night.

The former Club Brugge winger not only lost out to Matty Cash, but was also at the centre of Villa appeals for him to be sent off.

Tzolis had already been booked for a foul on Cash, when, in the 36th minute, he appeared to foul John McGinn as Villa broke from the edge of their own penalty area.

McGinn appealed that Tzolis should have been shown a second yellow card, but referee Jarred Gillett let the Arsenal man off the hook.

Arteta was wise to take Tzolis off at the break and his replacement, Eberechi Eze, had a hand in what proved to be Arsenal’s 59th-minute winner.

Eze slipped in Riccardo Calafiori and Saka got in front of Ian Maatsen to poke the Arsenal full-back’s low cross into the net. Saka’s goal had been the first shot on target in the game.

"It's a brilliant goal, it really is" 👏 Bukayo Saka gives Arsenal the lead at Villa Park! pic.twitter.com/aV7DA8cARL

Just before the goal, Arsenal thought they had been awarded a penalty. Ross Barkley lost possession with a sloppy pass, allowing Declan Rice to advance towards the Villa penalty area. He played the ball through for Saka and Maatsen barged into the back of the winger.

Gillett paused before pointing to the spot, but a VAR check showed that Maatsen’s foul had taken place outside the penalty area and Martin Odegaard fired the resulting free-kick wide.

The goal and the overturned penalty were pretty much it for Arsenal in terms of threatening the hosts, for whom goalkeeper Zion Suzuki made his debut. Suzuki did not have much to do with his hands, but impressed with his distribution.

It was Villa who went closest to scoring in the first half, through one of the club’s five surviving members of last season’s Europa League-winning team.

Emiliano Buendia scored Villa’s second goal in the final against Freiburg and the Argentine rattled the Arsenal crossbar with a 20-yard shot that had beaten visiting goalkeeper David Raya.

Before then, McGinn had sent a shot over Raya’s bar and into the building site where Villa are redeveloping the club’s old North Stand.

Buendia, McGinn, Cash, Pau Torres and Victor Lindelof are the only Villa players to have started the Europa League final who have not left this summer.

Defender Ezri Konsa is one of Villa’s Europa League winners to have departed and he made his Arsenal debut as a late substitute. The defender received a mixed reception, as he was first booed by some home fans but was then applauded.

Other than hitting the bar in the opening 45 minutes, Villa squandered a chance for a quick reply to Arsenal’s opener when McGinn hesitated instead of shooting after being played in by Nicolas Jackson.

Jackson lasted 71 minutes for Villa in what proved to be a promising debut. In the first half, he raced away down the right before sending the ball across the six-yard box. But there was no team-mate on hand to convert.

One of Villa’s other summer signings, Alejandro Garnacho, is yet to make an impact for his new club. The Argentine got an earful from manager Unai Emery for not being ready to go on. He eventually replaced Ross Barkley, but could not help conjure an equaliser.

This is the start Arteta wanted. But, in attacking positions, Arsenal will finish the transfer window weaker than they started it if the club are not active in the final hours of the transfer window. And that could prove costly.

We lost. We competed well. They won the league last year. We are trying to build a team but a lot of positive things [beyond] the result. How we competed. How it was progressively better. We didn’t create clear chances. Some players made fantastic debuts. Suzuki and Jackson did very good work. I think it’s the first step forward and positive for the next matches.

Accepting this result, I think we had chances to draw the match but we are in our rebuild. It is the way [ahead for us] making these changes and I say to the supporters and players that the message is there in the way we played.

To lose one match is painful but after the pain we must try to get positive things, This is the reason I am optimistic. There are 38 matches we played two. We haven’t one point but we can get better hopefully. And we will get players [Mbaye and Harwood-Bellis].

We can feel confidence because how we want to build the team again is true, to compete like today.

I think the squad we have now is how we planned with the  players we wanted.

[Are you confident you have replaced the quality that has gone?] Yes.

I’m really happy. It’s a big win. It’s a tough place to come and earn the three points but I think we deserved it.

It was a game where 11 was not enough and the finishers came in and did a magnificent job to win it. I know how tough it is to win here.

Every big team struggles against them for the past four years because they are so good. They are well coached, have great players. Great in transition. The moment you lose the ball and let them run inside they are really dangerous but I love a lot of the things I saw from my team.

Ebs [Eze] creates the action that sees us win the game, Bruno with Mikel [Merino] in midfield changed the dynamic of it, Ezri [Konsa] really composed and calm with every decision he made and then Zubi… I’m really happy with all of them.

Every game in the Premier League it’s like [you’re saying] we have to win this game. We know the level. We know how difficult it is in this league.

[Can you sign Julian Alvarez tomorrow?] I don’t know. That’s for the people upstairs.

It was a very tough match. Aston Villa’s defensive setup made things difficult for us, constantly catching us offside. We couldn’t attack as comfortably as we did last week. But as you know, sometimes one goal is enough for us. We have a very strong defence.

Today, we were great out of possession too and didn’t allow transition attacks.

I keep my targets for myself. Every week I want to be there and try decide the game as that’s what I’m in the team to do. That’s my mentality.

[Have you seen Chelsea?] I’ve seen them. [What do you think?] We’ll see on Sunday.

Jamie Carragher explains how Arsenal broke Aston Villa down for their winning goal 🔎 pic.twitter.com/CAI8zhznrJ

Arsenal host Chelsea on Sunday at 4.30pm while Villa go to Hull City at 5.30pm on Saturday. It’s too early for a must-win game for Villa who showed some positive signs tonight but they could certainly do with one.

Arsenal win with a performance of efficiency and patience that emphasises their superiority when asked to grind out a result.

John McGinnis arguing the toss with the referee about his belief that he was fouled in the box in the dying seconds. It was outside the box and if Maatsen’s ‘tackle’ wasn’t a foul, neither was Gabriel’s.

Not sure the way of refereeing that lets a lot of calls go and waits for VAR is going to enhance the game.

Maatsen tackles Bruno Guimaraes in the Villa box with an ugly lunge in which he appears to scissor him, kicking his heel with one leg before knocking the ball away with the other but the referee deems it fair and VAR lets it pass, too.

Arsenal’s game management is working well as usual until Raya goes too long and the ball bounces through to Suzuki. But when he starts a counter-attack Alysson ends it with a dive and back come Arsenal.

Maatsen slides in late on Saka down the right, bypasses the ball and crashes into his shin. Yellow card.

Aston Villa probe but Arsenal hold them 30 yards from goal and when they do slide pass down the side of a defender for Buendia to chase, Bruno is ideally positioned to cover and make the block which he celebrates as if he were Leonardo Bonucci.

Eight minutes of stoppage time are signalled by the fourth official.

Suzuki races 15 yards outside his box to head a long pass away from Havertz to McGinn. Back come Arsenal after McGinn is squeezed off the ball but Wan-Bisska wins it back with a fine tackle. He is among the best one-on-one pure defenders in the league.

Zubimendi rattles Buendia’s bones in a crunching but legal tackle.

That was Rice’s last contribution as he limps off. He is probably OK but wise to withdraw him if he has had a twinge.

Maatsen drives down the left and cuts into the box. White leans into him, Rice guides him with a rigid left arm and the rampaging left-back loses his feet. Maatsen acknowledges Rice’s fine defending when he gets back up.

Quite a few outside observers questioned why Arsenal signed Konsa. This apparent injury to Mosquera is the reason. With Saliba out for months and Timber still struggling to regain his fitness, Mosquera was the only right-sided centre-back in the squad (unless they repurposed White, who is needed at right back).

Garnacho faces up Saka after being played down the left by Buendia but his cross is blocked by the goalscorer. Raya catches the resulting corner.

McGinn wipes out Merino from behind and is deservedly booked. Moments earlier Alysson was also booked for leaving one on Gabriel after the centre-half had cleared the ball, choosing not to put on the brakes and bodychecking him instead.

Unai Emery has just gone ballistic at substitute Alejandro Garnacho.

Emery clearly wasn’t happy with Garnacho not being ready to come on and let the Chelsea loanee know about it.

And Mosquera cannot continue having overstretched so it’s a debut for the former Villa stalwart who is greeted warmly.

Suzuki saves in a one-on-one with Havertz running through from 40 yards, waiting and refusing to go down and make things easy for Havertz, sticking up a right arm to block the shot. But he may have been offside which may mitiagte it in terms of not costing Arsenal anything but he really should have beaten the keeper.

Nice pass from Merino to set the hare running.

Barkley plays a diagonal pass across the turf out to Alysson on the right and he hares round Calafiori to cross from the byline but could not get the ball past Gabriel at the near post.

Now Maatsen goes flying but this time in the Arsenal box under a challenge from White that was a duplicate of the one 30 seconds before. ‘Premier League corrupt as f---,’ sing the Villa fans, ignoring the similarities between the two incidents. The defenders’ arms made contact with the attacking players but without the force to send them sprawling.

Havertz hits the deck in the Villa penalty area when challenged by Kamara as they fought for Odegaard’s scooped dink from the right.

Bruno Guimaraes and Mikel Merino are stripped and ready to come on.

Once again, it’s Riccardo Calafiori who opens up the opposition’s defence with his off-the-ball running. He is the one player in this Arsenal team who makes genuinely unpredictable and unexpected movements.

McGinn’s combination with Jackson looks promising and the centre-forward invites him to bullock forward down the inside-right channel with a clever pass but the Villa captain is soon swamped by yellow shirts and the ball gets stuck beneath his feet.

Gary Neville makes the fair point that one of Arsenal’s most unheralded qualities is their patience. Their confidence in their rock-solid defence does not make them reckless but they are always confident of finding a way. They trust the method implicitly.

Aston Villa 0 Arsenal 1 (Saka) Mosquera has the ball 25 yards out, left of centre, he strokes it to Eze who angles a pass to Calafiori running between Cash and Lindelof. He makes it to the byline and cuts back a low cross that Saka and Maatsen both lunge at and the Arsenal winger gets there first to turn it in.

"It's a brilliant goal, it really is" 👏 Bukayo Saka gives Arsenal the lead at Villa Park! pic.twitter.com/aV7DA8cARL

Rice, Eze and Odegaard stand over it. Rive walks away and Odegaard approaches the ball with a semi-circular run-up. He whips it over the wall and about a foot wide of the left post. Suzuki was stranded but no matter.

It was outside the box. Not all that sure it was a foul either. But Arsenal will have a free-kick.

Maatsen and Saka collide as they chase a Rice pass that Saka would never reach. Seemed to be outside the box.

It has been fairly dull fare so far as two systems and structures that cede little space clash.

Lindelof rises high to meet Rice;s dipping cross from the right as Havertz, on his shoulder, was poised to pounce. He heads it straight up and Suzuki leaps to catch it.

Now Barkley picks out a diagonal to send Jackson down the left. The centre-forward reaches the 18-yard line, cuts inside and works it over to McGinn who lofts a cross over Villa’s back-post runners and out of play.

Eze did his best work from the left last season. Villa start with Barkley scoop-chipping a pass from the middle out to the left, 40 yards upfield. Maatsen runs on to it and drives past White to ram a shot into the side-netting.

Arsenal were too slow to move the ball forward in that first half, and too loose with it when they did get into promising positions. There’s a lack of urgency in their passing. I wonder if we’ll see Bruno Guimarães soon… one of the reasons they signed him was to add more quick forward passing to their play.

Signs of encouragement for Villa without creating much while Arsenal have been stymied so far by Villa’s neutering of Tzolis and the left wing. Arsenal’s right-sided trio – White, Odegaard and Saka – look the most likely to create something.

Only a minute of added time to be played. Arsenal still lacking a spark, largely because there’s a lack of precision in their forward, line-breaking passing.

Villa will be very happy with this half. Much more like their old selves in terms of structure and organisation.

Calafiori’s throw to Gabriel is picked off by Jackson down the right and he dribbles down the right. He is forced to slow down to wait for a midfield runner. When Hemmings catches up, so have three Arsenal defenders and though Jackson bends in a low, cross to the edge of the six-yard box it is about 18 inches away from Hemmings’ reach.

Calafiori goes down in the Villa box when Pau Torres uses his arm to lever him away as they tracked the flight of a cross. The referee sees nothing wring in it and neither does VAR.

Gillett takes an age to stop the play when Cash uses his body to shove Tzolis over after the winger had played a pass. Cash obviously thinks he has rattled the new signing and is keen to rough him up some more. The ref does award a free-kick but only after that daft delay.

Tzolis loses the ball on the edge of the Villa penalty area, tackled by McGinn. The captain slots a straight pass up to Buendia who tries to bend a pass into Jackson’s stride as he sprinted down the inside right channel but Gabriel read the trajectory and got there first.

Suzuki picks out McGinn with a long pass. He feeds it to Buendia who gives Hemmings a chance to chase it down the left. Arsenal shuffle over in defence so he doubles back and returns the ball to Buendia. The No 10 whips over a dipping cross looking for Barkley and Jackson but Calafiori and Raya make sure the goalkeeper wins it.

We’ve not seen much from Christos Tzolis on Arsenal’s left wing so far. He’s been excellent since joining the club this summer but he’s hardly seen the ball in this opening half an hour and he’s just been booked after losing a battle with Matty Cash.

Arsenal free-kick 30 yards out, left of centre, for a foul on Lewis-Skelly who was artfully shielding the ball. Odegaard chips to the right post but Havertz heads it back across the box rather than going for goal and Villa clear.

Cash gets the better of Tzolis again in the tackle and then Suzuki sprays a perfect 60-yard pass out to Hemmings that Gary Neville, likening it to something Ederson was capable of delivering for Man City, one of the best goalkeeper passes he has ever seen. Tzolis was booked for stopping Cash running off with the ball.

Maatsen, who could never dislodge Digne for long, has a chance now to make the position his won. He strides down the left, exploiting Rice’s positioning error but his right-foot isn’t half as good as his left and his bending effort is scuffed far too straight and easily cleared.

Saka drives down the right after a neat Odegaard, Saka, White triangle. Pau Torres races over to toe the ball behind for a corner. Saka takes and Rice flicks it on at the near post and Suzuki tips it over. No corner, though, as Gabriel had rag-dolled McGinn at the back post after the Villa captain had backed in to him and tried to stop him making a run into the middle.

“Champions of Europe, you’ll never sing that.” Villa fans poke the wound.

Arsenal are finding it difficult to play through the middle of the pitch but have found Saka in space on the right wing on a few occasions already. Villa are congesting the central areas, where Odegaard does his best work.

Calafiori picks off Kamara’s pass looking, for the third or fourth time, to play someone, usually Jackson, in behind the left-back. A minute later Calafiori challenges McGinn for a bouncing, loose ball and stoops to use his head. colliding with McGinn’s boot. Was the head low or the boot high? Arsenal think the latter but the ref sides, rightly, with McGinn.

Arsenal corner on the left. The threat inherent every time Rice is in a quadrant diminished on this occasion because Mosquera barged Cash just after Rice struck the ball. Free-kick to Villa.

Timber may be preferred by Arteta at right-back but Saka prefers White. The two have a well-grooved partnership in tersm of who underlaps and who overlaps. They never seem to get in each other’s way.

Bukayo Saka does seem to be getting a lot of time and space on the right flank.

It’s looking a risky tactic by Villa at the moment as the England international is being invited to cut in towards the penalty area.

Havertz is played down the inside-right channel in the penalty area by a cute Odegaard pass bur he blazes his shot across goal and wide of the left post. A replay shows he was offside but even so it was a lazy finish.

Kamara grabs Tzolis round the waist from behind and when the winger hits the deck, rounds him and passus to Buendia who crashes a right-foot diagonal shot on to the bar from 20 yards. The ref did not see it as a foul despite Arsenal’s protestations but had it gone in it would have given VAR a dilemma.

Worth keeping an eye on Aston Villa midfielder George Hemmings tonight.

He is only a teenager and has emerged from Villa’s academy, but Unai Emery is already a huge fan.

Hemmings produced a highly promising performance in the Super Cup against Paris Saint-Germain earlier this month.

Suzuki misjudges the flight of Rice’s typically menacing corner and flaps at it but his defenders and an offside flag leave him without egg on his face.

McGinn stops Calafiori down the left then gives the ball straight to Tzolis. The Greece winger opens his body and passes to Lewis-Skelly who shoots with his right foot from the left of the 18-yard line. Cash slides in to block the shot and it loops over the bar for a corner.

Hemmings uses his strength to hold off Ben White and shift the ball inside to McGinn who wraps his left instep around a shot and wafts it into building site behind Raya’s goal.

Ibrahim Mbaye and Taylor Harwood-Bellis are in the directors’ box watching the game. Villa don’t look like a hastily assembled team.

Suzuki knocks the ball long with his left foot, looking for Jackson but the ball spins away from him to Raya who boots it back upfield. McGinn pounces on it, turns past Rice and plays Cash in down the right. He crosses towards the near post and Mosquera hooks it clear.

Arsenal kick off with Odegaard spinning and trying to play Saka in down the right as they defend the empty North Stand end. The ball skids off the turf and Saka can’t trap it. The ball goes out for a Villa throw-in.

Who dies in the summer and played for both clubs.

Arsenal are in fact in yellow and navy. My mistake.

Villa in claret and blue with a twist, the shorts are blue for the first time since, I think 2001. Arsenal are in yellow and black. Leeds, like Arsenal, have traditionally worn yellow and blue as their away strip but have been shunted into yellow and black as well by Adidas this season.

There are a few guys standing in the North Stand with hard hats on, and it appears they are on ball retrieval duty.

They will be on red alert for any wayward shots that land in the empty stand.

Warm reception for Ezri Konsa from Villa’s fans as he walked back to the tunnel with Arsenal’s substitutes.

Konsa joined Arsenal last week for £51m, ending a spell of seven years at Villa Park.

Wonder if the likes of Morgan Rogers and Emiliano Martinez will get a similar reception when they return here with Chelsea.

Zion Suzuki is one of two debuts for Aston Villa tonight and there is a genuine buzz of excitement around the Japan international.

Suzuki was signed from Parma for £30m as the replacement for Emiliano Martinez and arrives with a stellar reputation.

He’s got big boots – and gloves – to fill, but Unai Emery is convinced he will become a future star at Villa Park.

The other debutant is record £65m signing Nicolas Jackson, who joined last week from Chelsea.

Good evening. Yes, the first match was not as planned but we must keep going forward. Today we are playing our first home match and I am looking forward. Aston Villa are in a transition period and rebuilding on and off the field.

Unai Emery’s 2.0 have been under construction all summer and there could be 10 new signings in by tomorrow morning.

The North Stand at Villa Park, which faces the iconic Holte End, is also under renovation and closed down for tonight’s game.

We have had a real block of training sessions to work on things and prepare for this game in the right way.

We will have time to make changes throughout the game [on why he has picked an unchanged team]. They did really well [against Coventry] and for the game we expect [tonight] they have the right qualities to hurt them and that’s how we start.

They have that [upheaval in personnel] but they have been with Unai for a long time, they are a super well-coached team and we know how tough it is always to come here. We are very conscious of that but also very ambitious.

That’s the way we want to play [with aggression] constantly from the first minute, to suffocate the opponent and be better than them.

[Does it being your 250th Arsenal Premier League game add something special to it?] Just to win [makes it special].

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League match between Aston Villa and Arsenal from Villa Park. The champions travel to the team that finished fourth last season in buoyant mood and form despite some misgivings within their fanbase about their recruitment this summer.

It amounts so far to making Pier Hincapié‘s loan into a proper transfer, revamping the left wing with Christos Tzolis replacing Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli, upgrading options in central midfield by buying Bruno Guimarães and selling Cristian Norgaard – and signing Ezri Konsa from today’s opponents to give them the greatest elite defensive depth that I can recall at club since Manchester City’s Treble winners had Kyle Walker, Ruben Dias, John Stones, Nathan Aké, João Cancelo, Aymeric Laporte, Manuel Akanji, Rico Lewis and Sergio Gómez on the books at the same time.

Villa, by contrast, have endured a turbulent summer of trading with the departures of Europa League winners Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans, Lucas Digne, the aforementioned Konsa, Ollie Watkins and Emi Martínez, raising, along with other departures, more than £315m. They have spent about £180m to remodel the team though Johan Manzambi, who is injured, and João Gomes, who is suspended after his red card in the 4-0 defeat by Brighton, are absent tonight.

We can expect to see Zion Suzuki, Matteo Ruggeri and hopefully Nicolas Jackson and Leon Goretzka who have been registered in time to play, plus the loan signings Aaron Wan-Bissaka and Alejandro Garnacho. Still to come are the pending purchases of Taylor Harwood-Bellis and Ibrahim Mbaye in a process that emphasises how profoundly Villa are invested in and dependent upon their manager, Unai Emery.

After so much upheaval, it would be foolish to set much store on Villa’s 2-1 victory last season, sealed by Emi Buendía’s winner in the fifth minute of stoppage time. Arsenal barely broke sweat in blowing Man City away in the Community Shield and cakewalked to victory over Coventry in the league’s opening fixture. His past work suggests Emery will be able to forge another formidable side from his talented new squad but this match feels two months too soon for him against his old club.

#1705. GdS: How Amorim’s fluidity helped Rabiot record career-best start to a season

Adrien Rabiot continues to deliver in the biggest games for AC Milan, and Ruben Amorim is arguably getting the best ever form out of him.

La Gazzetta dello Sport begin a report by recalling how different things were in the summer. With Milan falling to fifth and Massmiliano Allegri being sacked, many presumed that Rabiot could follow him to Napoli, to play Champions League football.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Rabiot not only remained at Milanello, but is also the Atlas of the team this year. He carries it on his shoulders and takes its weight with disarming ease and personality. While Allegri observes Milan from below, Adrien has found a new coach who is giving him a new lease of life.

The derby goal is an excellent indicator of Rabiot’s confidence, attempting that billiard-like shot (even though some, like Yunus Musah, maintain it was a cross) in a match like this, with the game still wide open, signifies complete self-confidence.

The Frenchman knows perfectly well he has a powerful shot, but he opted for finesse, guiding the ball to kiss the post and land in the back of the net as eleven Nerazzurri players watched it slowly and mockingly cross their penalty area.

Rabiot was one of the derby’s heroes but has been performing at a high level for several matches now. He currently has the best average rating in the squad, and it’s a stratospheric 6.81 (out of 10, across all games).

The other key number is nine: five goals and four assists this season makes nine contributions, the most in the squad. In the league, he’s been involved in a goal in each of his last five games: assists against Lazio, goals against Lecce and Sassuolo, a goal and assist against Atalanta, and a goal in the derby.

To better understand his further improvement from an already very high level, we must consider that in the entire last season, Adrien had six goals and four assists. He’s one goal away from matching that tally.

Some tactical considerations help contextualise things. Compared to Allegri, Amorim’s style of football is on another level, being much more attacking. It’s not based solely on counter-attacks, but on a flow of play that starts from midfield and allows for the runs of those who move in between the lines.

Rabiot has always been a player who can get forward: he has the physique, technique, and footballing intelligence. Amorim has given him a further step because he’s made him more difficult to read for opponents.

If before, the Frenchman was a classic pivot midfielder, now you find him practically everywhere. At the start of the season, Amorim’s style of football was positional, locked into a 3-4-2-1 that seemed set in stone with Rabiot behind the striker.

Then the Portuguese coach realised he was doing himself harm and began a tactical overhaul. The fundamentalist has become fluid, and the playing system is now an abstract concept that must be filled with individual interpretations.

This is a set of circumstances where Rabiot shines. The derby is a perfect example: the former PSG man was everywhere, depending on his own tendencies and the team’s need for certain characteristics in certain parts if the pitch.

This is the best start to a season of his career. Now, in addition to the pitch, he’ll also have to keep an eye on his desk. After Strahinja Pavlovic and Christian Pulisic, he’s the next one destined to ascend to the fourth floor of Casa Milan to sign a renewal waiting for him.

#1704. Report: Future of £16m Liverpool star revealed as 'uncertainty' emerges

Liverpool are currently fifth in the Premier League.

This is the same position that they ended the 2025-26 season in and what resulted in Arne Slot being sacked.

Indeed, we're only a few months into the new campaign at the moment but, fans would have probably hoped to see some more signs of improvement than what they've been shown thus far.

Of course, it may take some players longer than others to get adjusted to Andoni Iraola's ways but, if they don't get back and track and start working their way back up the table soon, some serious questions will need to be asked.

The futures of many Liverpool players are currently being discussed and now, an update has emerged about one of the Anfield outfit's men.

Wataru Endo is 'certainly' going to leave Liverpool in 2027

Several members of Liverpool's first-team squad have their contracts expiring in June 2027.

Alisson, Wataru Endo and Virgil van Dijk are just a select few who could end up exiting L4 this summer.

No discussions about extending the contract of any of the aforementioned trio have taken place yet with the Liverpool ECHO now sharing their latest information about the future of Endo.

"Endo will certainly leave the Reds in 2027," they wrote.

"He is out of contract next summer with the only uncertainty being whether he departs in January or sees out his deal and leaves on a free transfer."

Liverpool must decide whether they need to keep Wataru Endo at Anfield until the end of the season

When Endo was first signed by Jurgen Klopp back in 2023 for £16 million, he was seen as a bit of an out there signing.

The deal for the Japanese international came out of nowhere and went against almost every transfer strategy that Liverpool had adopted during the years prior.

However, he fit right into Klopp's plans and was even seen as his 'closer' after a few months into being a Liverpool player.

Wherever the midfielder was needed on the pitch, he always put in as much effort as possible but, after his injury last season, things just haven't been the same.

He's had no playing time under Iraola and, even though the Spaniard said he'd get his chance this term, that doesn't feel all that likely now.

So, with the January transfer window coming up, the Reds must decide whether they think they can complete the season without him among their ranks.

If they can, they should try their best to find him an exit route and allow him to see his final years as a footballer out as a regular starter, rather than a bench-warmer.

Obviously, the Reds are going to lose money on his exit but, since he's now 33 years old, Endo's next transfer is likely to be his last before retirement.

#1703. Celta Vigo vs Union SG - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 03 Nov 2026 18:49, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 18:52

Celta Vigo will continue their Europa League league stage campaign with a home fixture against an in-form Union SG outfit on Thursday evening.

The La Liga outfit are currently 25th in the overall table, picking up three points from three matches, while Union SG are sixth, collecting seven points from three games.

Celta made a disappointing start to their 2026-27 Europa League league stage campaign, losing 1-0 away to Omonia, before going down 2-1 at home to Juventus, but they managed to post a 2-1 victory over Celtic last time out to move onto three points, which has left them in 25th.

The Sky Blues will enter this match off the back of a 3-0 defeat to Rayo Vallecano in La Liga, with the result leaving them 10th in their domestic table.

Claudio Giraldez's side have games to come against Bournemouth, Marseille, H. Beer Sheva and Lillestrom before the end of their league stage, and it would be a surprise if they were eliminated in this round of the tournament given their quality.

Celta reached the quarter-finals of the 2025-26 Europa League, losing to German outfit Freiburg, while they were also present in the semi-finals back in 2016-17, being beaten by Manchester United on that occasion.

Home advantage could count for a lot on Thursday, but Celta will be welcoming a Union SG outfit that are currently in excellent form.

Indeed, the visitors have posted four straight wins in all competitions, including a 2-1 victory over Beveren in their last match on October 31.

Union SG have seven points on the board from their three Europa League matches this season, meanwhile, which has left them sixth in the overall table on seven points.

David Hubert's side opened their Europa League campaign with a 3-0 victory over Viktoria Plzen, before drawing 1-1 with Real Sociedad in their second match, with that result coming ahead of a 4-0 success over H. Beer Sheva last time out.

Union SG played in the 2025-26 Champions League, finishing 27th in the league stage, while they reached the knockout round playoffs of the 2024-25 Europa League.

The Old Lady will also take on Lech, Lyon, Besiktas and Celtic before the Europa League league stage draws to a close.

Celta will be without the services of Carl Starfelt, Miguel Roman, Alvaro Nunez and Borja Iglesias through injury on Thursday night.

Javi Rodriguez is actually the team's leading goalscorer this season, scoring three times in 10 appearances, and the 23-year-old will feature in defence.

There should also again be a spot through the middle for Ferran Jutgla, who has netted twice in 14 appearances during the 2026-27 campaign.

Union SG, meanwhile, will be without the services of Kevin Mac Allister, Fedde Leysen, Ondrej Kricfalusi, Rob Schoofs, Mateo Biondic and Ilan Hurtevent for Thursday's game through injury.

Guilherme Smith has been in strong form this season, scoring five goals and registering two assists in 16 appearances, and he will feature in an attacking area.

Meanwhile, there should be a spot in the final third for Relebohile Mofokeng, who has five goals and four assists in all competitions this season.

Radu; Rodriguez, Caceres, Alonso; Rueda, Febas, Burcio, Carreira; Aspas, Jutgla, Alvarez

Koffi; Chibani, Sylla, Havenaar; Van De Perre; Patris, Olaru, Zeneli, Guilherme Smith; Biondic, Mofokeng

Celta will have home advantage on Thursday, but we are struggling to back them with any real confidence in this match given Union SG's form, ultimately settling on a low-scoring draw.

#1702. Incredible, 3 fantastic stars now reportedly picking between Liverpool and Chelsea

Liverpool and Chelsea are set to do battle in the transfer market. Not just one but three stars are set to pick between the two.

The nature of elite clubs right now means you'll battle against them for virtually every player. After all, stockpiling talent is the order of the day - even if it's entirely unclear whether that actually works.

Clubs are signing elite stars that they don't necessarily need, just on the chance that they might end up better than what they've already got. It feels like a massive waste of money, really, but maybe that's why I'm not a sporting director.

But to be fair, sometimes the needs of top clubs simply align. That's certainly the case with Chelsea and Liverpool, both of whom saw similar problems crop up in the summer without clear solutions.

Midfield is the obvious area. Both Liverpool and Chelsea sold key midfielders (Curtis Jones and Enzo Fernandez) without replacements. It's a situation that pits the two of them against one another as they chase signings to fill the gaps.

Liverpool vs Chelsea but in the transfer marketThere are two main midfielders on the market right now who quite clearly interest both Liverpool and Chelsea. The most obvious is Lamine Camara, who is expected to leave AS Monaco in 2027. Of course, he was expected to leave in 2026 and Chelsea thought they had a deal all but done at the deadline. Camara and Monaco backed out last minute, however, and now Football Insider is one of many outlets reporting that Liverpool have stolen a march in the race.

There are two main midfielders on the market right now who quite clearly interest both Liverpool and Chelsea. The most obvious is Lamine Camara, who is expected to leave AS Monaco in 2027.

Of course, he was expected to leave in 2026 and Chelsea thought they had a deal all but done at the deadline. Camara and Monaco backed out last minute, however, and now Football Insider is one of many outlets reporting that Liverpool have stolen a march in the race.

#1700. Revealed: SIX Man United stars named in combined XI with Chelsea despite Michael Carrick's side's nightmare start - as stats boffins pick Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans over Moises Caicedo

Published: 03:01 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 05:44 EDT, 31 October 2026

As matchweek nine of this enthralling Premier League season rolls around we have a host of excellent games to look forward to this weekend.

Champions Arsenal will look to bounce back after a humiliating defeat away to Fleetwood in midweek but will have to travel to Anfield and take on a Liverpool side who look to have finally hit form, winning their last five games in all competitions.

Manchester City welcome third place Brighton, who have been the surprise package of the season so far. There is a London derby as Tottenham take on Crystal Palace.

Perhaps the most anticipated game is the 12:30 Saturday kick off between old rivals Chelsea and Manchester United.

The once perennial title challengers both find themselves struggling so far this season, albeit United much more so, and will be desperate to pick up three points.

Sofascore have put together a combined XI of the best-performing players from both squads, with average ratings accrued from all competitions this campaign. So, who has made the cut? Daily Mail Sport takes a look.

Between the sticks is Manchester United's big Belgian, Senne Lammens. The 24-year-old has been a breath of fresh air at Old Trafford after United after the struggles of his predecessor Andre Onana.

Onana who had some memorably poor performances in both the Champions League and Premier League during his two year spell in Manchester.

Lammens appears to have dropped off in form slightly from the end of last season but has still been solid considering his club's shocking form.

He gets the nod ahead of his Belgian compatriot Mike Penders who has had a tricky first few games in blue, and Emi Martinez who is still sidelined with a head injury he sustained away at Everton.

Senne Lammens is yet to keep a clean sheet in the Premier League this season as United have conceded 13 goals already

The first of our three central defenders is Chelsea's £70million man, Wesley Fofana.

A big-money signing from Leicester City in 2022, Fofana has only really begun to make regular appearances for Chelsea in the past year and has been a fixture when fit in Xabi Alonso's back-three system, starting all four games he has played.

Despite a number of lacklustre performances, most recently a nightmare at Anfield in midweek, overall the Frenchman has looked solid, winning 66 per cent of his defensive duels and 70 per cent of his aerial battles.

Playing through the middle of our back three is Harry Maguire.

Nobody in Manchester United's leaky defence has truly shone this season with the Red Devils already conceding 13 goals in the Premier League and six in the Champions League.

Nevertheless Maguire makes the cut, partially due to both sides not having performed at the back this season. Maguire has improved in possession hugely, registering a 90 per cent pass completion rate and a 100 per cent dribble success score.

Lisandro Martinez completes our defence despite his recent controversy.

Earlier this month Martinez found himself in hot water after making some serious criticism of Manchester United's transfer business - or lack of - and sporting director Jason Wilcox, but his personal performances have remained steady.

The Argentine scored a freakish own-goal away to Fulham in a 1-1 draw in September but has for the most part avoided any major errors at the back and certainly cannot be blamed for United's catastrophic start to the season.

When veteran Jordan Henderson was brought in over the summer many fans assumed he would play a bit-part role. Instead, the 36-year-old has become a regular starter for Alonso's team.

The Englishman has started every game for Chelsea since making his debut against Brentford and has been excellent, especially at home to Bournemouth in which he bagged a brace in a rampant 5-1 win.

Questions will be asked over whether he will be able to sustain this form over the course of the season given his age but for now he makes it into our XI with the highest average rating out of the lot.

The former Liverpool skipper as been a revelation at the Bridge this season, the only question is whether he keeps it up

Partnering Henderson is another Englishman who has rediscovered form this season but under different circumstances.

After a period out of favour with ex-manager Ruben Amorim, Kobbie Mainoo became the catalyst in his side's stellar end to last season. But this campaign his lack of ‘dynamism’ has been criticised by former player and now pundit Gary Neville.

Many have questioned if a midfield two of Mainoo and Youri Tielemans is sustainable due to the pair having similar profiles, and a combination of Mainoo and Carlos Baleba lacks experience.

Carrick has stuck with Mainoo thus far and individually he has earned solid ratings. He beats out Chelsea's Moises Caicedo to a place in the XI.

Pedro Neto has transformed his game under his new gaffer as an auxiliary wing-back.

The Portuguese has enjoyed his best start to a season at Chelsea since he joined the club for £65m back in 2024, scoring four and assisting one in eight games for the Blues so far.

He has also looked capable defensively in his new wing-back role in Chelsea's 3-4-2-1 formation with 55 defensive contributions and 29 ball recoveries this season.

If some places in this team are close calls, there is no questioning this man's inclusion. The Blues' £117m summer acquisition has so far looked worth every penny, lighting up the Premier League as one third of Chelsea's deadly front three.

The England star has five goals and has provided five assists in all competitions this campaign and appears to be that final piece of quality Chelsea have so desperately needed in attack.

Rogers has enjoyed a number of particularly memorable performances including his relentless showing at home to Leeds, where he assisted four goals, as well as his outing against Bournemouth in which he ran the game for 80 minutes and scored one.

Best friends Morgan Rogers (right) and Cole Palmer (left) also make the combined XI

At the beginning of the season, Bruno Fernandes would have been nailed on for this combined XI.

Just 12 games in, his inclusion may surprise a few. There is no questioning the man's ability but there have been serious concerns over whether his actions reflect what is expected of a United captain.

Fernandes has been very outspoken about the state of the club and the management of the squad and has subsequently had 'clear-the-air' talks with his boss.

The Portuguese international remains, however, one of the most talented midfielders in the Premier League and even with all of his issues off the pitch, he continues to contribute on it with four goals and one assist in all competitions.

Bruno Fernandes was benched for United's 3-0 loss at home to Bournemouth but is back in for Saturday's visit to Chelsea

One has to feel a bit for Youri Tielemans. As a top talent entering the twilight of his career he has walked into an absolute car crash at Old Trafford.

And he has gone from a stellar season getting Champions League football with Aston Villa to sixteenth place with United in October. He is yet to wow the Stretford End.

Similarly to Kobbie Mainoo, the midfielder has been critiqued for his lack of running, with United sat third from bottom in the rankings when it comes to ground covered.

All the same, he has registered 371 passes - well above the league average - and has a completion rate of 89 per cent.

It is safe to say we are unlikely to see Palmer play up front this season but to fit the Blues' talisman in we have had to put him up top.

With Palmer fresh off the back of his first red card in senior football in Chelsea's 2-0 home defeat by Tottenham, it is easy to forget the start the Englishman has had to this campaign.

Seemingly energised after his omission from England's World Cup squad, the forward has looked back to his best at times.

He has racked up four goals and three assists so far and will be desperate to make an impact on his return from suspension against his boyhood club.

Despite suggestions otherwise, Markus Krösche could still work with Timmo Hardung at AC Milan, despite the latter earning a promotion.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The duo are credited almost completely with the work done across recent years and the Rossoneri have always had an interest in hiring both. Yet, it seemed that it would be impossible recently, thanks to Hardung moving into Krösche’s old role. But that may not be the case.

According to Matteo Moretto, the German could still head to Italy – with Krösche – despite his new role with Frankfurt, as MilanNews relays from his appearance on Fabrizio Romano’s YouTube channel.

“Despite Milan’s denials, Krosche will be the club’s new Head of Football. I also want to clarify the possible role of Timmo Hardung, sporting director of Eintracht Frankfurt. Timmo Hardung is Krosche’s right-hand man, with whom he has been working for some time.

“The Frankfurt club has confirmed him within the structure, but it is not 100% certain that he will remain in Germany. Milan is sticking with him, Krosche holds him in high regard, and it cannot be ruled out that Milan could also make an attempt for him in the coming weeks.

“Krösche will have to fit into a structure that is already tested, the one built and designed by Gerry Cardinale, however, I don’t rule out that in the coming months, if the opportunity arises, perhaps Milan could also try for Hardung.

“Krösche has great respect for Hardung and considers him extremely well-prepared for his role.”

If Gerry Cardinale could bring both to Casa Milan, it would be a huge statement from him. It would also say a lot about the future of the project.

#1695. Trabzonspor vs Freiburg - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Cole | 03 Nov 2026 19:56

Unbeaten in the 2026-27 UEFA Conference League so far, Trabzonspor will look to maintain their perfect record when they welcome Freiburg to Papara Park on Thursday.

The Turkish side have collected six points from their opening two league-phase fixtures and arrive on the back of seven consecutive victories across all competitions, while the visitors have recovered from a difficult spell with successive domestic wins ahead of their trip to Turkey.

Trabzonspor have emerged as one of the Conference League's early pace-setters under Thomas Reis, with their impressive domestic form translating into European success.

The Black Sea Storm began their continental campaign with an entertaining 4-2 victory away to KuPS, before returning to Papara Park to beat Hearts 2-0 on matchday two.

Those results came either side of an equally encouraging 2-0 home victory over Besiktas in the Super Lig, while subsequent league wins against Caykur Rizespor (4-3) and Gaziantep (2-0) have extended their winning sequence to seven matches.

Trabzonspor have six consecutive victories at Papara Park, and they have a significant European milestone within reach if they make it seven in a row, as a third successive victory in major continental competition would represent their best such run since November 2013.

Winning their opening three matches of a European campaign would also be only the second time they have achieved that feat, and they will hope to do just that in what will be their first ever meeting against the visitors.

However, Freiburg should provide a considerably different examination from Trabzonspor's previous European opponents.

The German side reached last season's Europa League final before losing to Aston Villa in Istanbul, and their experience at a higher level of continental competition means they should not be underestimated despite their inconsistent beginning to this campaign.

Julian Schuster's side opened their Conference League campaign with a 3-2 victory over Jablonec, but their trip to Monaco proved considerably more difficult, as they suffered a 3-0 defeat, which they followed with a 3-1 loss to Bayern Munich in the Bundesliga.

However, their domestic performances improved, with a 3-2 victory over Wolfsburg in the DFB-Pokal followed by a 2-1 away success against Augsburg.

Nevertheless, their European away record remains a concern, having lost four of their previous five matches on the road in continental competition.

Trabzonspor have several selection concerns heading into Thursday's encounter, with Aral Simsir, Franculino, Arseniy Batagov, Ruslan Malinovskyi and Okay Yokuslu among those expected to miss out.

Cihan Canak and goalkeeper Onuralp Cevikkan are also doubts, while Sidny Lopes Cabral is suspended following his dismissal against Hearts.

Paul Onuachu is another player whose involvement requires monitoring, although the Nigerian forward returned to the starting lineup against Gaziantep after missing two league matches through injury.

Freiburg are expected to be without Philipp Treu, who is struggling with an ankle injury, while Florent Muslija remains sidelined with a cruciate ligament injury.

Schuster should nevertheless have considerable experience available in central defence through Matthias Ginter and Philipp Lienhart, while Maximilian Eggestein and Yannik Engelhardt are options in midfield.

Vincenzo Grifo, Yuito Suzuki and Jan-Niklas Beste could provide the creativity behind Igor Matanovic, who has scored in each of Freiburg's last two matches.

Onana; Pina, Nwaiwu, Savic, Eskihellac; Fabinho, Kabasakal; Salah, Muci, Saviolo; Onuachu

Backhaus; Kubler, Ginter, Lienhart, Makengo; Eggestein, Engelhardt; Beste, Suzuki, Scherhant; Matanovic

Trabzonspor's outstanding home form, attacking consistency and confidence from seven consecutive victories make them difficult to oppose, particularly against a Freiburg side that have struggled to reproduce their domestic performances in European away fixtures.

#1694. Opinion: Liverpool's golden chance to steal brilliant star and leave Arsenal in shock

Liverpool have an incredible chance to steal a fantastic player. It's a move that would leave Arsenal in absolute shock.

Liverpool's attack is not what it should be. There are many reasons for this, but struggling to create good opportunities when you've dropped this much money is ridiculous.

It's a sign that this wasn't a particularly good recruitment process. Either Liverpool signed the wrong players, or the wrong players for their coach, or the wrong players for one another.

That latter reason is the one we believe in. This isn't a balanced group of forwards and it's pretty clear to see. They've struggled under two head coaches now but we know they're good players.

So the balance just isn't right. It's quite easy to see why, too, given no one in the group is left-footed and the point of attack is always exactly the same no matter who's on the pitch. Liverpool are ultimately very easy to defend against and have a complete inability to shake things up.

That's why we think they should go out and buy one last attacker for this group. With the added bonus of it destabilising Arsenal.

Endrick for Liverpool, not Endrick for ArsenalAnfield Watch understands, along with most other outlets, that Liverpool tried to sign Endrick in the summer. There was some sort of approach but one that fell on deaf ears. Now, the Reds were far from the only club that tried to sign him. Endrick just wasn’t interested in leaving Real Madrid as he felt he could force his way into the picture. That hasn’t really happened - he’s played 78 La Liga minutes as of writing. José Mourinho keeps winning matches in charge, too, and that’s with a very settled forward line, all of whom are performing. It’s very difficult to see how Endrick gets back in - especially as Carlos Espi rivals him for minutes as a substitute.

Anfield Watch understands, along with most other outlets, that Liverpool tried to sign Endrick in the summer. There was some sort of approach but one that fell on deaf ears.

Now, the Reds were far from the only club that tried to sign him. Endrick just wasn’t interested in leaving Real Madrid as he felt he could force his way into the picture. That hasn’t really happened - he’s played 78 La Liga minutes as of writing.

José Mourinho keeps winning matches in charge, too, and that’s with a very settled forward line, all of whom are performing. It’s very difficult to see how Endrick gets back in - especially as Carlos Espi rivals him for minutes as a substitute.

TeamTalk claims that the Brazilian is now more open to moving and it’s alerted Arsenal. The Gunners also tried to sign Endrick in the summer and are willing to continue their pursuit.

But we really, really think Liverpool should be on this one. Endrick’s data at Lyon last season was exceptional and our Value Adder model had him down as a truly fantastic player.

He’s also a left-footed forward who can cover through the middle or wide on the right. In other words, he plays the two positions where Liverpool genuinely lack balance.

And if Endrick truly is Arsenal’s big attacking play in the transfer market, grabbing him would shock them enough to provide an extra win for Liverpool. It’s the kind of move they should be making - and we hope it can be forced into reality.

#1691. Cole Palmer and Man United unpacked: The truth about Old Trafford links, why he really got a new Chelsea deal, Xabi Alonso's 'emotional control' advice after red card and how he must step up against 'Big Six' rivals

Published: 08:00 EDT, 30 October 2026 | Updated: 05:46 EDT, 31 October 2026

Despite the speculation snowballing in the second half of last season – and it was as if there had been an explosion at a rumour mill – Manchester United never did come in for Cole Palmer.

No conversations were held with Chelsea in the summer. Not about him, anyway. United negotiated for Andrey Santos. It took two days to agree that deal, worth £48million plus £2m in easily achievable bonuses and with Chelsea retaining a 10 per cent sell-on clause.

But according to sources with knowledge of those talks and any others which occurred in that window, Palmer’s name was not mentioned whenever officials from both clubs, such as Chelsea sporting director, Paul Winstanley, and United director of football, Jason Wilcox, spoke.

Which might surprise a few. Because it was said Manchester United wanted Cole Palmer and Cole Palmer wanted Manchester United. Apparently he missed Manchester, could no longer stand London, was tired of waiting for Chelsea to be good again and thought he belonged in the Champions League. He was the boyhood United fan who grew up worshipping Wayne Rooney.

That was what we were seeing while scrolling social media in the build-up to a summer when England manager Thomas Tuchel excluded the 24-year-old from his World Cup squad.

In fairness, the original suggestion that Palmer might be interested in United was not plucked out of thin air. It is said that at least one person close to Palmer's circle was happy to stand up those suggestions.

Cole Palmer returns from suspension for Saturday's match against Manchester United, the club he was linked with in the summer

Palmer's red card against Tottenham last weekend was the first of his career

Daily Mail Sport has also learned one former United legend who dabbles in media work was likewise privately claiming he knew Palmer fancied the move. This came at a time when it was unclear whether Bruno Fernandes would be staying or sold to Saudi Arabia.

Yet nothing happened, and now, tomorrow at Stamford Bridge, Fernandes will return from the naughty step to represent United, and Palmer from his one-game suspension to play for Chelsea.

Chelsea had insisted all along that Palmer was untouchable. They even handed him another improved contract earlier this month, despite his last season not reaching the standards he had set for himself.

He ended an injury-interrupted 2025-26 with 11 goal involvements in the Premier League, after securing 23 in the previous season, and 33 before that.

When asked for the reasoning behind that new deal – whether it followed interest in him from a rival or was to provide parity after the £117million signing of Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa – Chelsea sources described it as a desire to lock down one of their best players.

He was already contracted to 2033. Now he is tied to 2034 on a nicer salary. Nobody in the Premier League has a longer contract, though as Chelsea head into another challenging game against a ‘Big Six’ side, Palmer could do with earning his pay rise.

We have seen this playmaker step up on occasion, usually when there is a trophy for winning.

Palmer signed an improved contract at Chelsea earlier this month despite a below-par campaign last season

In the 2025 Club World Cup final, where he made Paris Saint-Germain’s superstars seem mediocre compared to him. In the Conference League final of that same year, where Palmer had a ‘sod it’ moment as he turned on his creativity, telling us afterwards that he was sick of going backwards and sideways, as per Enzo Maresca’s patience-first philosophy.

Yet these glimpses of his genius have been fleeting in the Premier League’s most high-pressured matches. In 27 games versus Chelsea’s ‘Big Six’ opponents, Palmer has scored only two non-penalty goals.

Both of those arrived against United in his very first season when Mauricio Pochettino got the best out of him.

That is not to disregard the eight penalties he has dispatched which displayed his willingness to embrace extreme psychological pressure from 12 yards.

But statistically, his goals per 90, assists per 90, shots per 90 and chances created per 90 all decrease when playing Arsenal, Liverpool, Manchester City, United or Tottenham Hotspur, compared to his Premier League output overall ever since signing for Chelsea in 2023.

He has had a fun time toying with Spurs on occasion, but not last weekend. Palmer was deservedly shown two yellows in that 2-0 defeat, Chelsea’s first home loss to their rivals since 2018 – one for barging into Mateus Fernandes, and the other for standing on Conor Gallagher’s ankle.

We get it – he was frustrated, feeding on scraps, hardly ever in the game. But this was a flashback to the ill-discipline which plagued Chelsea’s previous campaign under Maresca.

In the 2025 Club World Cup final, Palmer made Paris Saint-Germain’s superstars seem mediocre compared to him

With Joao Pedro sidelined, Chelsea need Palmer to step up now that he is back from his ban

There was nothing cool to that performance from a player who now sells his own ice cubes – it's £3.50 for four pieces shaped like footballs if interested – and Alonso privately reminded him afterwards about the importance of emotional control. Palmer apologised.

It was the first red card of his career, and the first shown to a Chelsea player since Alonso took charge in the summer, with Palmer suspended for their Carabao Cup penalty shootout loss to Liverpool on Wednesday. Another opportunity at a trophy slipped away at Anfield.

With Joao Pedro sidelined – and no specific date set for his return from a knee injury – Chelsea need Palmer to step up now that he is back from his ban.

Against the United team that a fair few thought he could be joining in the summer would be as good a time as any to repay Chelsea’s faith and begin banishing the ‘Big Six’ narrative attached to his name.

#1690. Report: Liverpool make contact over enormous Trent Alexander-Arnold return

Trent Alexander-Arnold to Liverpool might actually be real. Reports claim contact has been made over an enormous return.

Speculation that Trent Alexander-Arnold may one day return to Liverpool has been around since before he'd even left the club. Talk that he was leaving kicked off a year in advance, after all, and there was always half a sense that he'd be back at some stage.

However, we then all witnessed how he left. The lack of any acknowledgment from his side that he would leave, the claiming it was a last-minute decision, the comments, the attitude - it felt like disrespect to a lot of people.

So why a possible return? The thinking has long been that this was a deal that worked out for absolutely no one. Alexander-Arnold is not a starting player for Real Madrid and, in fact, he's not even their second-choice right-back at the moment.

The Ballon d'Or isn't on its way, in other words.

Whereas Liverpool completely failed to replace him. They have zero production from right-back now as they've decided that actually-a-centre-back Ronald Araujo is their best option, at least while Conor Bradley is out injured.

And Real Madrid? They're paying big wages to a player they're not actually using. Which brings us to the latest update out of Spain.

Trent Alexander-Arnold to LiverpoolCadena SER reports that Liverpool have made initial contact about a move for Alexander-Arnold. This would apparently be a loan move in January - perhaps just an initial one before something more permanent (although that's just speculation on our part). But they claim that Liverpool asked Alexander-Arnold's representatives about a possible return. It's entirely unclear what response they got to that, however, and we can't be sure that the player would even want it. After all, that's quite an incredible step back after everything. An admittance of defeat, really.

But they claim that Liverpool asked Alexander-Arnold's representatives about a possible return. It's entirely unclear what response they got to that, however, and we can't be sure that the player would even want it.

Not that he'd be the first. The parallels with Michael Owen are incredible - an academy product lured by Real Madrid, who didn't break into the starting XI, and then wanted a return before getting anywhere near the end of his contract there.

Owen ultimately didn't get that return as Liverpool couldn't afford him. He had to settle for Newcastle United, though did hold out hope of eventually returning to Anfield.

Alexander-Arnold might actually get his wish, though. Liverpool need a right-back. Real Madrid need to shed a right-back. The player needs to play where he knows he can thrive.

All signs do point to Anfield, admittedly.

#1687. Report: Julian Ward has decided, massive Liverpool deal could now actually happen

A huge decision has been made, and now a massive Liverpool deal could actually be happening.

Being a sporting director comes with a lot of pressures in modern football. It was a role that didn't necessarily exist in this form two decades ago.

But now, the sporting director is probably the most important position at a football club. They have to make the big decisions when it comes to the club's recruitment. They decide who and when to get rid of the coaching department and oversee numerous staff within the club.

It's an unrelenting job that also comes with a lot of scrutiny in the media.

Richard Hughes experienced that first-hand, with many proclaiming him as the reason for Liverpool's failures. His successor, Julian Ward, will want to run things differently.

Julian Ward's big decisions at LiverpoolComing into this role at this particular time makes things even more difficult for Ward. Liverpool are embarking on a huge change both on the pitch and off it. FSG have just sold a minority stake to the 1892 Holdings consortium led by Amit Bhatia. There is an option to convert that into a majority stake in the coming years ahead. With the likes of Jeff Bezos involved, there is a strong possibility that Liverpool could come under new leadership in the near future. At the same time, the squad is undergoing a metamorphosis. Liverpool are rebuilding their team after a successful decade under Jurgen Klopp. Ward's task will be to recruit the key building blocks of this rebuild and ensure Liverpool bring in the right players in order to put together a team ready to compete at the upper echelons of world football.

Coming into this role at this particular time makes things even more difficult for Ward.

#1686. Barcelona vs. Aston Villa: Lamine Yamal breaks Kylian Mbappe scoring record in Champions League

By Ben Knapton | 03 Nov 2026 20:21, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 20:33

Barcelona winger Lamine Yamal has broken a Kylian Mbappe Champions League record courtesy of his opening goal against Aston Villa.

The 19-year-old phenom unsurprisingly started on the right-hand side of the Blaugrana attack at Camp Nou, and he took just seven minutes to make his mark.

However, Yamal was gifted his historic goal on this occasion, as Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki played a short ball to the under pressure Joao Gomes, who passed straight to Yamal.

The Spain international took the ball under his spell and curled in a fine strike to put La Blaugrana ahead, in turn becoming the highest-scoring teenager in Champions League history.

Yamal came into the game level with Mbappe on 13 Champions League goals before turning 20, but the Barcelona phenom has now surpassed his Real Madrid counterpart.

Aston Villa make a mistake at the back and Lamine Yamal makes them pay inside 10 minutes ⚡ ? Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max: https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB https://t.co/1IcWOPMJlt

Yamal has amassed his 14 Champions League goals in 37 games in the competition, in addition to providing as many assists since making his debut in September 2023.

The attacker failed to score in his first season in the tournament, but he found the back of the net five times in the 2024-25 edition as Barcelona progressed to the semi-finals.

Yamal then enjoyed his best scoring season in the Champions League to date in the 2025-26 campaign, netting six times, but he was unable to prevent Barca from exiting in the quarter-finals.

This season, Yamal has already struck three times in Europe's premier tournament, also bagging against Feyenoord and Paris Saint-Germain before breaking Mbappe's record against Villa.

At his current scoring rate, Yamal is averaging 0.38 goals per game in the Champions League, and the 19-year-old could very well continue at the top continental level for more than 15 years.

If the Barcelona prodigy continues finding the net at the same volume in the Champions League, he could end his career with around 80 UCL goals with approximately 210 appearances.

Such a total would currently place Yamal fifth in the Champions League all-time scoring charts, only behind Cristiano Ronaldo (140), Lionel Messi (129), Robert Lewandowski (109) and Karim Benzema (90).

However, Mbappe is currently on 73 goals of his own, and the Real Madrid marksman will almost certainly surpass the 80 mark in due course barring a catastrophe.

#1685. Man City sign Enzo Fernandez for £125m to end transfer saga of the summer

Manchester City have equalled the British record transfer on deadline day after agreeing to pay £125m to sign midfielder Enzo Fernández from Chelsea.

The deal brings to an end the biggest saga of the summer and means that Enzo Maresca, the new City head coach, has landed his number one target.

City left it until the last day of the transfer window to strike an agreement after Chelsea decided that Fernández’s exit was in the best interests of the club. But a late move to replace the Argentine with Monaco midfielder Lamie Camara collapsed to the anger of the Premier League club, leaving Xabi Alonso one player light among his midfield options.

Having refused to meet Chelsea’s self-imposed deadline to sign Fernández for £120m earlier in the summer, City had to equal the £125m Liverpool paid Newcastle United for Alexander Isak 12 months earlier.

Fernández had made it clear that he wanted to leave Chelsea some time ago and was left out of Alonso’s squad for the victories last week over Luton Town, in the Carabao Cup, and Brighton.

Having initially wanted to join Real Madrid, Fernández set his heart on linking back up with Maresca at City. The pair share a close relationship and had kept in touch after Maresca left Chelsea at the start of the year.

This is the second time Fernández has become the most expensive player in British transfer history, having previously set the record when he joined Chelsea for £107m from Benfica in the 2023 winter window.

Introducing our new Argentinian Blue 🇦🇷🩵 pic.twitter.com/nEHQ1oM855

During his time at Chelsea, 25-year-old Fernández won the Club World Cup and the Europa Conference League but he was also at the centre of controversy.

In January 2025, Fernández posted a video of himself and some of his Argentina international team-mates singing an offensive song about France players of African origin after winning the Copa America. He apologised to his Chelsea team-mates and made a donation to an anti-discrimination charity, but was still made the team’s vice-captain.

Last season was Fernández’s best goalscoring campaign, as he netted 15 goals in all competitions for Chelsea but the club finished 10th in the Premier League table. In April, he was suspended for two games by the club for suggesting he would like to live in Madrid – which was perceived as a come and get me plea to Real Madrid.

He angered England fans with his celebration after scoring against Thomas Tuchel’s team in Argentina’s World Cup semi-final victory over England, before being sent-off in the final defeat by Spain.

Chelsea fans booed Fernández in pre-season, although the club’s travelling supporters sang his name when he was introduced as a substitute in the victory over Fulham at the start of this season.

Fernández thanked his team-mates and the Chelsea staff in an emotional farewell post on Instagram. He added: “I want you to know that these have not been easy days for me. Writing this is not easy either. The truth is, I haven’t been in a good place.

“Three years ago, Cobham and Stamford Bridge became home for me and my family. I grew attached to the people, to the shirt, and to the badge of this incredible club.

“Believe me when I say that, from the moment I arrived, I became obsessed with winning and with bringing this club every trophy that its history deserves. We suffered, we cried, I got angry many times, but we also celebrated titles and unforgettable victories. Together, through the good times and the difficult ones.

“I live football the same way I live my life: with passion and with all my heart. That is why I want you to know that I understand you. I truly understand you, from the bottom of my heart.

“But life is about making decisions, and right now I find myself having to make one of those difficult decisions. I’ve said it before, but I want to say it again: I have grown incredibly fond of this club. Chelsea will always have a place in my thoughts and, above all, in my heart.

“But I also understand how football works. I know how passionate you are, because I am the same. And if I were in your position, I would probably be thinking the same way.”

Proper City 🤩🩵 pic.twitter.com/TfRTZOnPrw

The sale of Fernández means that Chelsea have set a new British transfer record of their own, having secured more than £500m in sales and loan fees during the summer transfer window.

Chelsea set about spending some of the money made from the Fernández sale by agreeing a last-minute deal for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara.

Monaco had rejected a bid of £38.5m from Chelsea on deadline day, but an improved offer of £47m was accepted late on Tuesday night, only to be called off by Monaco on the stroke of the 11pm deadline.

Chelsea had been able to complete a medical during negotiations and Camara agreed to a six-year contract with the option of a further year to bolster Alonso’s midfield options, but he will now not join the club.

Chelsea had also seen at least one offer for Bournemouth’s Alex Scott rejected this summer, while the club showed an interest in Roma’s Manu Kone and explored whether or not a move for Arsenal’s Martin Zubimendi would be possible earlier this month.

Chilly tonight... pic.twitter.com/VihgKCScfn

“We had been aware of Chema’s potential for sometime, and we are delighted to welcome him to the club, and look forward to working with him.”

Fernandez says: “Manchester City are the most successful club in England in recent times.

“Every player wants to be part of a club like this because everyone knows how well-run City are.

“I could not be happier to be here, and I am ready for the challenge of helping City continue winning trophies. This is a club built for success.

“If you look across the squad, City have quality in every area. I want to learn from my new teammates and become a better player.

Sunderland were involved in the most bewildering transfer of the summer on deadline day as they fought a day-long tug-of-war with Crystal Palace for winger Malick Fofana.

On a day of claims and counterclaims, Sunderland have finally triumphed in the battle to land the Belgium international just an hour before the deadline.

But despite their success, it was a transfer that will leave a sour taste in the mouth to many, with the player repeatedly changing his mind about which club he wanted to join

As the saga dragged on, it is understood Fofana had a medical in Lyon with both Sunderland and Crystal Palace given access to the information as he still could not decide which club to join as talks continued into the evening.

Sunderland had a bid of around £25m accepted by Lyon on Tuesday morning and thought they had an agreement with both the player and his agent on personal terms and fees only for Palace to make a late attempt to hijack the deal.

The London club’s manager, Pierre Sage, who worked with Fofana at Lyon, is thought to have personally intervened in an attempt to persuade the player to move to South London. By late afternoon, Palace appeared to have got their man having also offered more money to Lyon and higher wages to the player and fees to his agency.

Sunderland, though, refused to concede defeat and, according to reports in France, launched a counter proposal of their own led by French owners Kyril Louis-Dreyfus who flew to Lyon to try and clinch the deal.

At one stage, it was even claimed that the player had two different private jets waiting at the airport to take him to either London or the North East depending on who he elected to sign for.

That was later refuted, although it is understood the player did have a medical in Lyon that could be viewed by both clubs before he made up his mind. That gave his representatives more time to thrash the terms of a deal with both clubs.

However, having failed to board an earlier flight to Lyon after talks with Palace advanced, Sunderland’s late push belatedly persuaded the 21-year-old to head to Wearside, and he is due to be unveiled on Wednesday morning.

Arsenal had also been linked with the player earlier this week but were not willing to match the asking price for Fofana who they viewed as a project player.

Crystal Palace are having a frantic end to the transfer window, with Ben Chilwell also a deal they are pursuing.

The former England left-back, 29, is at Strasbourg where he is in the final year of his contract. Palace are also trying for Quinten Timber from Marseille and are still in the race for Lyon’s Malick Fofana.

Ethan Nwaneri has completed his loan move from Arsenal to Borussia Dortmund. A lot of Arsenal fans will be pleased he hasn’t been sold, which was a real possibility this summer. Hopefully this move is more successful than his time in Marseille in the second half of last season, when the chaos at the club did not help the teenager to settle.

Liverpool’s last significant business for the window is done with the completion of the £30m deal for goalkeeper Lucca Brughmans from Genk. The 18-year-old will remain in Belgium, to play the season with his current club.

He has been bought with the future in mind and Liverpool are covering all bases, as Alisson Becker – who has been the undisputed No 1 since he arrived in 2018 – is now in the final year of his contract. Liverpool also spent £33m on Giorgi Mamardashvili last summer.

Alisson could have left this summer, with Juventus initially keen to sign him. Either way, this points to Liverpool making plans for a new generation.

Never quite lived up to his billing as a Berbatov-Havertz hybrid, scoring 11 goals in 53 appearances for Newcastle in all competitions last season when the idea of him leading the line was slowly abandoned. Serie A should suit him better, and Newcastle have confirmed his move to Italy.
