Davis is getting a fair bit of joy down Ipswich’s left and the ball has been on to him quite a few times. He is being afforded too much space by Liverpool to get crosses in.

Andoni Iraola is bringing on Nyoni for Mac Allister, who was on a booking.

Davis is found making a run in behind and his cross from the left side of the box is blocked by Araujo and goes behind for a corner. Lukic’s delivery is headed away at the front post by Gravenberch.

Double change for Ipswich as McAteer and Ouattara replace Fatawau and Palacios.

Barcola drives down Liverpool’s left and, as he approaches the Ipswich box, cuts onto his right and feeds it across to Gakpo, whose shot misses the target.

The ball comes to Flemming on the edge of the box and he tries to curl one into the far corner but it is an easy save for Alisson.

Barcola is nearly played in behind but Scherpen does really to get out of his goal quickly and gets to the ball first, just ahead of Barcola.

Davis and Ipswich can count themselves very, very lucky. It would have been a penalty but Szoboszlai was offside when the original ball was played. For the second time tonight, an offside call massively goes in Ipswich’s favour; one to deny Isak a hat-trick and now to deny Liverpool a penalty. A massive let-off for Ipswich.

#IPSLIV – 68'VAR recommended an on-field review for a potential penalty, but determined that Szoboszlai was in an offside position in the build-up.REF: "After review, there's a penalty shout on Szoboszlai. However, in the build-up to the penalty shout, Szoboszlai is in an… pic.twitter.com/DN4i8rj5fg

Liverpool are demanding a penalty. Szoboszlai is played in behind and is constantly having his shirt pulled by Davis. Davis then appears to bring Szoboszlai down inside the box but the referee waves it away. Davis gets none of the ball and the referee is being sent to the screen...

Barcola’s first few touches in a Liverpool shirt are pretty good down the left. He is playing in his most natural position of wide left, with Gakpo now down the middle and Szoboszlai on the right.

Gary O’Neil is going to make a double change as Clarke and Flemming come on, with the latter making his debut. Maeda and Emersonn come off.

So, here comes from the £123m Frenchman as Barcola enters the fray for his Liverpool debut. Gravenberch also comes on. There will be no first Liverpool hat-trick for Isak as he heads off, as does Munoz.

Bradley Barcola comes on to make his Liverpool debut! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/PjO78nlcqj

Andoni Iraola must be ripping his air out with the lack of composure and control from his side since half-time. It is no wonder he is about to turn to his bench and a certain Frenchman.

Enciso is given far too much space to drive towards the Liverpool box before shooting but Alisson makes the save. Liverpool, despite being 2-0 up, have showed a real lack of composure since the break.

If trends are anything to go by, Bradley Barcola will be introduced in the next three or four minutes. Andoni Iraola likes to change things around the hour mark and if the Frenchman warms up anymore, he will nearly overheat.

Kerkez is the latest player into the book for a foul on Fatawu.

Fatawu receives it out on the right for Ipswich and cuts inside onto his preferred left foot before curling an effort towards the far post but it goes wide.

Jacquet takes a heavy touch from a high ball and ends up taking out Emersonn, which earns the Frenchman a booking.

Liverpool work it well down their left as Isak plays it into Gakpo, who drives towards the Ipswich box. He plays it across the face of the penalty area to Szboszblai, who flicks it first time into the path of Wirtz. The German’s effort takes a deflection and goes behind for a corner.

Szoboszlai’s outswinger finds a free Mac Allister at the front post but the Argentine’s header is straight at Scherpen. That was a good chance for Mac Allister.

We are back under way at Portman Road. No changes for either side at the break.

We have just seen replays of a possible penalty shout for Liverpool right at the end of the first half for a foul on Gakpo by Fatawu and it looked a decent shout.

Possession: Ipswich 41%-59% LiverpoolShots: 8-7Shots on target: 2-6Corners: 3-2Touches in opposition box: 7-12

Perhaps if Liverpool were playing a team with a bit more savvy, the 2-0 scoreline they currently protect would have been in jeopardy. Ipswich have put some nice moves together and had half chances but not enough to really turn the screw. Andoni Iraola, certainly, has been unhappy at times and it is becoming a trademark to see him spin around from the technical area in disgust when a ball has been squandered. In the main, though, he can be satisfied with this opening 45 minutes. Liverpool should be winning from here.

The first half is brought to an end at Portman Road and Isak’s quickfire double early in the half gives Liverpool a 2-0 lead at the break.

Wirtz feeds a lovely pass into the left channel to pick out the run of Isak into the Ipswich box but Diop comes in with a crucial challenge.

Two added minutes at the end of this first half.

Araujo slices a clearance out of play for an Ipswich corner. A real gift for the home side as Araujo was not under any real pressure.

Isak should head away at the near post but it comes to Mac Allister to clear away.

A chance for Wirtz as the ball falls to the German on the edge of the Ipswich box but his shot is saved by Scherpen down to his left.

Enciso is the first Ipswich player into the book tonight for delaying a restart.

Szoboszlai, for the third time in the half, shoots from range. Again, the Hungarian gets plenty of power on it but fortunately for Scherpen it is straight at him.

Enciso turns neatly not far outside the Liverpool box and then shoots but slices the shot a fair way wide.

Tommy Elphick, a member of Andoni Iraola’s coaching staff, is booked for his protestations. Liverpool are not happy with some of the fouls being given against them and then some that are not given for them, including a clear foul from Emersonn on Van Dijk that was not penalised.

Isak has the ball in the Ipswich net for the third time tonight and thinks he has his hat-trick but the offside flag goes up. It comes from a stunning piece of play from Wirtz down Liverpool’s left, taking up a pocket of space and taking the ball on the turn beautifully. He then spots Isak in space at the far post and picks him out perfectly, with Isak slotting home. However, the offside flag is up and replays prove he was just offside. Could Isak have timed his run just fractionally better and still reached the cross? Probably but it was very close.

Mac Allister receives a pass from Wirtz and, from just outside the box, decides to shoot but his effort goes just over. Scherpen did appear to have it covered anyway.

A crucial intervention from Araujo. Enciso drives down Ipswich’s right after Fatawu’s header, with Mac Allister tracking back. From the right side of the Liverpool box, Enciso’s deflected cross comes towards Maeda at the far post but Araujo makes an important clearance.

Moments later, Davis again meets a Fatawu cross at the far post but his header is off target.

Fatawu’s dangerous cross from the right all the way to the back post finds Davis, who heads back across goal. Emersonn takes a touch with his chest on the edge of the six-yard box before shooting but Jacquet is on hand to make a crucial block. Ipswich though do have their first corner of the game.

Lukic clips it in and Alisson should punch away with ease. However, the ball comes off Gakpo and, very fortunately for Alisson, the ball gets trapped between his own legs and he can gather. Alisson will be a relieved man.

Szoboszlai sends another powerful shot from range towards the goal and forces Scherpen into another decent save. Ipswich are not helping themselves at times by just giving the ball away inside their own half.

Szoboszlai comes close to adding a third for Liverpool. Fatawu inexplicably gives the ball away inside his own half before Mac Allister plays it forward to Szoboszlai, who takes just one touch before firing towards goal. Scherpen gets down well to his right to make the save.

And there he is. You have been waiting 12 months to see the Alexander Isak of Newcastle play for Liverpool but here he is, a confident, instinctive-finishing menace. His first goal was marvellous, his second was a work of art, given the pass from Cody Gakpo, and what a position Liverpool have put themselves in to get their first win under Andoni Iraola. And, while we are at it, Gakpo has made both Liverpool’s goals: what on earth were they doing thinking of selling him to Manchester City?

Isak, on his last trip to Portman Road, scored a hat-trick for Newcastle here in a 4-0 win back in December 2024. He already has two goals to his name tonight inside the opening quarter of an hour.

Emersonn misses from close range for Ipswich but the offside flag goes up against Greaves. It was a bad miss from Emersonn but Greaves, who had delivered the cross for Emersonn, was offside.

The first booking of the game goes the way of Mac Allister, who is booked slightly harshly for a foul on Enciso.

Moments later, Ipswich have their first effort of the game but Fatawu curls over from the edge of the box.

Another fine goal from Isak and Liverpool lead 2-0 not even 10 minutes into this game. It is Gakpo who assists again with a superb pass with the outside of his right foot from halfway into the left channel to pick out the run in behind of Isak. The Swede cuts inside Greaves onto his right before then chopping back onto his left. He then coolly slots home past Scherpen and Liverpool have the dream start.

Inside NINE minutes Alexander Isak has two goals! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/3UGq0bwqRm

Liverpool take a deserved lead at Portman Road. Kerkez wins the ball back for Liverpool on halfway and the ball comes to Gakpo. The Dutchman drives forward and spots Isak in space to his right. Isak’s movement is very clever as he drifts off the defender into space. He takes a touch before smashing the ball past Scherpen at his near post. Should Scherpen have saved that? Possibly but Isak did hit that very hard. For the first time this season, Liverpool lead in a Premier League match.

A blistering finish from Alexander Isak! 💥 pic.twitter.com/jSGlIZsQtA

Wirtz is penalised for a very soft foul on Enciso, who just threw his hands in the air after the slightest bits of contact. The referee Darren England was not initially going to give it but eventually does, giving Ipswich the chance to swing it in from the left into the Liverpool penalty area.

Fatawu swings it in with his left but Alisson punches away.

It has been all Liverpool in these early stages but have yet to have a shot. Ipswich have barely touched the ball thus far.

Liverpool win the first corner of the game as Davis is forced to put it behind after good work from Munoz down Liverpool’s right.

Szoboszlai’s outswinger is headed away from danger.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel at Portman Road and we are moments away from kick-off. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

Ipswich: Scherpen, O’Shea, Diop, Greaves, Davis, Palacios, Lukic, Fatawu, Enciso, Maeda, Emersonn.Substitutes: Walton, Furlong, Kipre, Ouattara, Florentino, Nunez, McAteer, Clarke, Flemming.

Liverpool: Alisson; Jacquet, Araujo, Van Dijk, Kerkez; Mac Allister, Szoboszlai, Wirtz; Munoz, Isak, Gakpo.Substitutes: Mamardashvili, Endo, Tsimikas, Barcola, Frimpong, Gravenberch, Nyoni, Koumas, Ngumoha.

"Everyone's going to love him" 😍Jamie Redknapp is looking forward to seeing Bradley Barcola play for Liverpool this evening! pic.twitter.com/Ut9Zx4gbB2

The Paraguayan is in his second stint at Ipswich and has two assists to his name in the first two league games.

"He is the talisman already inside these first two games"Can Julio Enciso provide another assist tonight? 👀 pic.twitter.com/FaDkndt3BG

"I'm desperate for him to do well!" Jamie Redknapp says Florian Wirtz has to produce more for Liverpool right now 💭 pic.twitter.com/1fYT9t9tx3

A milestone appearance for Dom 🫰🔴 pic.twitter.com/C28iemsxou

"I really feel they've got that recruitment right' Luke Chambers says the Premier League experience of players that Ipswich have signed will be massive for them 🧠 pic.twitter.com/DgwYsTlHBD

“It gives us a big belief that we can compete at the level. Coming up from the Championship, there is always some doubt around. The home win over Sunderland was huge for us. And then to be in the game for as long as we were at Manchester United was impressive. I have challenged the lads a lot. We do not focus on the outcome or results, we just commit to being the best version of ourselves. We cannot go toe-to-toe with everyone. We have to be sensible and smart.”

Andoni Iraola has made a change at right-back tonight, with Ronaldu Araujo replacing Jeremie Frimpong. Araujo arrived at Liverpool this summer on loan with an option to buy from Barcelona.

A first Reds start for Ronald 💪 pic.twitter.com/P80pwhlBJ9

"He's ready, definitely we will use him in the second half" Andoni Iraola says Bradley Barcola has looked good in training and is hoping to give him some game time against Ipswich ⏳ pic.twitter.com/C00WVI7ACd

Andoni Iraola wondered what might happen when he first sat down to talk with Bradley Barcola.

Here was one of the world’s best wingers, with his 13 major honours, 28 international caps and £123m price tag – a combination that could easily lead a man to view himself through the prism of a superstar: never mind what I can do for you, what can you do for me?

Liverpool’s due diligence on Barcola had all been positive – not least from the currently injured Hugo Ekitike, who had been a vocal advocate of his compatriot’s capabilities to the recruitment team – but Iraola wanted to gauge for himself exactly what the 24-year-old was going to offer.

Ipswich were very active in the market upon their return to the Premier League, making 14 signings in total, with plenty of them involved tonight. Here is a sample of what Gary O’Neil’s side did during the window:

Liverpool: Alisson; Jacquet, Araujo, Van Dijk, Kerkez; Mac Allister, Szoboszlai, Wirtz; Munoz, Isak, GakpoSubstitutes: Mamardashvili, Endo, Tsimikas, Barcola, Frimpong, Gravenberch, Nyoni, Koumas, Ngumoha.

We are about to find out the two starting XIs at Portman Road. Will Bradley Barcola start for Liverpool on his debut?

The third matchday of the new Premier League season kicks off at Portman Road as newly-promoted Ipswich host Liverpool.

Andoni Iraola has drawn his first two games in charge of Liverpool, both 2-2 stalemates against Newcastle and Nottingham Forest respectively. Liverpool secured a move for forward Bradley Barcola from PSG in the final few days on the window for a fee that could rise to £123m and the Frenchman is set to make his Liverpool debut tonight.

“We are very happy with Bradley,” Iraola said. “He was our priority; to sign a very good player in that position. He has come with the right mentality. I like that he wanted Liverpool a lot, he just wanted to come here. That is a good first sign. Being the player he is and the things he has won recently, he has come with the willingness to help us. I am very happy with him.

“He trained well with us, and if everything goes well in today’s [Thursday] training, he will definitely be available for tomorrow [tonight]. He has trained with us three times. He has not had minutes in pre-season but he has been training normally with the group. It is a decision we have to make. We have to consider that he has not had minutes in pre-season.”

Liverpool won both fixtures when Ipswich were last in the Premier League two seasons ago, including a 2-0 win on the opening weekend in Arne Slot’s first game in charge of Liverpool as they went on to win the Premier League that season.

Ipswich won their first home game on their return to the Premier League, beating Sunderland 2-1 on the opening weekend. However, they fell to a 5-2 defeat in their first away game at Manchester United. Over the course of the summer transfer window, Ipswich made a total of 14 signings and spent over £200m.

“What we can do is perform in a way that always gives us a real chance, which we have done so far,” Ipswich boss Gary O’Neil said. “We were in that game at Manchester United until a couple of moments took it away from us. We were in it, so that is what we need to do, we need to make sure that no matter who it is, whether it is Liverpool, Manchester United, Manchester City, when they come to Portman Road, we need to make sure we are right in the game to give ourselves opportunities. We will always be a threat; we have scored four goals in two games. That is really good for a promoted side. We look a goal threat, and we need to keep that going and that will be tested.”

Team news from Portman Road to follow shortly.

#1661. GdS: ‘The mini Mourinho’ – Amorim’s assistant Fernandes having huge impact at Milan

Most of the best coaches in the world rely on those and it’s no different at AC Milan, with Ruben Amorim having a select group around him.

With Amorim, his coaching staff have always been a talking point. A close-knit bunch, the Portuguese brought them to Manchester and then Milano. Now, after the Derby della Madonnina, the focus is on one part of the team.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

As Gazzetta dello Sport writes, a lot of credit for this week has been given to Carlos Fernandes, Amorim’s right-hand man. The two met during Amorim’s playing days at Benfica, where the latter was working with the youth team.

From there, they discussed ideas and created a bond which took them to Casa Pia, then to Braga, Lisbon, Manchester and now Milano.

Nicknamed the ‘mini Mourinho’, Fernandes is not just a set-piece specialist – as his role may suggest – instead, he does much more. Indeed, he participates in analysis, training planning and much more. Amorim has even stated before that he’ll be a better coach than him, the Mourinho to his Bobby Robson.

For now, though, the pair work together and they are unbelievably close, as seen with the celebrations in the derby.

#1660. Opinion: Arsenal star should soon be starting for Liverpool as a world-class player

One Arsenal star is reportedly heading towards the exit door. Liverpool should make their move ASAP - he’d start for them.

Liverpool need to bolster their midfield - that's clear for all to see. They've built a group entirely out of progressive, attacking midfielders who want to play the no.8 role and paid little attention to those who can actually control the middle of the pitch.

We do expect that to change in 2027. Liverpool have been linked with some more control-focused midfielders. Some win the ball back, some maintain possession.

And that's what's necessary. The Reds have very little versatility in the middle - they're essentially setup to play one style of game and if that doesn't work, it's not easily changed.

Which should turn them towards an Arsenal star who looks near-certain to leave North London sometime soon. At least, turn them back towards that star.

Martin Zubimendi to LiverpoolLiverpool tried to sign Martin Zubimendi back in 2024 but he ultimately decided to stay put with Real Sociedad. By the time he was ready to move in 2025, the Reds have settled on a different midfield after winning the Premier League title and didn't want to invest in new players. That opened the door for Arsenal to swoop in and they did exactly that. Zubimendi signed for them that summer and went on to win the Premier League title last season as a starting player. However, they've quickly decided to move on from him. We assume that's because the Zubimendi and Declan Rice partnership was viewed as a little too defensive and a little immobile through the pitch.

Liverpool tried to sign Martin Zubimendi back in 2024 but he ultimately decided to stay put with Real Sociedad. By the time he was ready to move in 2025, the Reds have settled on a different midfield after winning the Premier League title and didn't want to invest in new players.

That opened the door for Arsenal to swoop in and they did exactly that. Zubimendi signed for them that summer and went on to win the Premier League title last season as a starting player.

However, they've quickly decided to move on from him. We assume that's because the Zubimendi and Declan Rice partnership was viewed as a little too defensive and a little immobile through the pitch.

Bruno Guimaraes joined from Newcastle United and now they're midfield is more attacking. Though, we think they've made a mistake there.

Zubimendi performs incredibly well on our Value Adder model but he went under the radar a bit. We have him as the second most valuable defensive midfielder in the Premier League, only for him to receive zero hype about it because no.1 was Rice.

That has TeamTalk reporting that Zubimendi is read to leave already as he's not getting first-team football when he really should be. And we think that Liverpool is where he should get it.

If Arsenal genuinely don't believe Zubimendi is good enough, Liverpool should snap him up to prove them wrong. After all, there's no reason not to sell a sub-par player to Anfield, is there?

We just don't believe he's actually sub-par. He's actually what Liverpool need in the middle of the pitch and if a deal is available, we're convinced they should go for it.

#1659. Levski Sofia vs Jagiellonia Bialystok - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sebastian Sternik | 03 Nov 2026 22:15

The Vasil Levski National Stadium will host Thursday’s Europa League clash between Bulgarian champions Levski Sofia and Polish outfit Jagiellonia Bialystok.

Both sides head into the encounter in good recent form, but a victory would provide a significant boost to their hopes of reaching the knockout stage.

Julio Velazquez is approaching his second anniversary at Levski Sofia, and the Spanish coach continues to impress since taking charge of the Bulgarian giants.

Levski are currently on a six-match unbeaten run across all competitions, winning four of those matches and scoring nine goals along the way.

Their last defeat came against Red Bull Salzburg in their Europa League opener, with the Bulgarian champions suffering a 1-0 loss in a game where they failed to register a single shot on target.

Remarkably, that was also their last outing on home turf, with Velazquez and his men embarking on a run of six consecutive away matches.

Even then, it was not their usual home ground, as Levski have been forced to relocate from the Georgi Asparuhov Stadium to the Vasil Levski National Stadium for their European fixtures.

Nevertheless, the Bulgarian champions will now be hoping to take another step towards reaching the knockout stage of a European competition for the first time since their memorable 2005-06 UEFA Cup campaign, when they reached the quarter-finals.

Jagiellonia Bialystok enter Thursday’s game on the back of a three-match winning run – a run which has brought some much-needed relief and stability for head coach Adrian Siemieniec.

September and October turned out to be challenging months, with Jaga enduring a run of seven defeats from nine games at one point.

Off the pitch, the club was also embroiled in major controversy after Siemieniec received a six-match ban and a €20,000 fine for contacting a match official ahead of the penultimate game of last season.

However, two Ekstraklasa wins and a 6-0 thrashing of Lechia Gdansk in the Polish Cup have lately boosted spirits in Bialystok, as the club look to make serious progress in Europe.

As things stand, Jaga remain just outside the top 24 in the Europa League after collecting three points from their opening three games.

Their 3-1 victory over Ararat-Armenia was sandwiched between a 2-1 defeat to Olympiacos and a painful 3-0 thrashing at the hands of Anderlecht a fortnight ago.

Jagiellonia will now hope to strengthen their hopes of reaching the knockout stage when they face Bulgarian opposition for the first time in their history.

Jagiellonia Bialystok Europa League form:

Jagiellonia Bialystok form (all competitions):

Brazilian forward Reinaldo will be Levski Sofia’s main goalscoring threat on Thursday, having registered two goals and an assist across his last two Europa League outings.

Fellow countryman Everton Bala also scored on his last appearance in Europe and is expected to start on Thursday.

The hosts will be without young midfielder Asen Mitkov, who has not featured since picking up an injury while on international duty.

Experienced forward Radoslav Kirilov is also out of action, having yet to make an appearance this season due to a knee injury.

Jagiellonia Bialystok, meanwhile, will be missing Norbert Wojtuszek, who has not made a single appearance since returning from international duty with an injury.

Star midfielder Jesus Imaz has scored in successive games, and he is fully expected to start on Thursday night.

Forward Nik Prelec has also found the net in consecutive matches and will be looking to continue his impressive start to life in Bialystok, having already contributed to nine goals this season.

Vutsov; Maicon, Makoun, Dimitrov, Neves; Everton Bala, Moubarik, Grujic, Soula; Reinaldo, Serginho

Jagiellonia Bialystok possible starting lineup:

Abramowicz; Montoia, Kobayashi, Vital, Conceicao; Lozano, Klynge, Imaz; Szmyt, Prelec, Sow

Both teams have got momentum after picking up positive results in recent times, and both will fancy their chances here.

Jagiellonia have scored nine goals across their last two away matches, and they have enough quality to cause Levski problems. Nevertheless, we are predicting a close encounter and backing a high-scoring draw.

#1658. Jamie Carragher issues apology for telling Aston Villa fans to 'shut the f*** up' - after club's owners threatened former Liverpool defender with legal action

Published: 08:57 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 11:21 EDT, 31 October 2026

Jamie Carragher has fronted up and apologised to Aston Villa and its supporters after his 'clumsy & wrong' language saw the club's owners threaten legal action.

The story took a dramatic turn on Friday night when Villa released a club statement revealing the bombshell claim that they intend to take legal action against Carragher.

In a statement on club channels carrying the name of co-owner Nassef Sawiris, Villa wrote: 'Aston Villa will initiate legal action against Jamie Carragher for his unacceptable insults about the Club and its fans.

'Aston Villa will not allow anyone to stop our ascension in English and European football. Nassef Sawiris, Chairman.'

The row, which centres on comments made by Carragher on the Overlap this week in which he pushed the idea of Unai Emery becoming the next Manchester United manager, only escalated further when Carragher doubled down, telling Villa fans to 'shut the f**k up'.

But the Liverpool legend changed his tune on Saturday afternoon in a bid to defuse an increasingly volatile situation.

I’d like to apologise to Aston Villa, the owners & their fans. My language this week was clumsy & wrong.I can assure Villa fans it was tongue in cheek but I can understand it’s not come across that way, so apologies. Good luck today UTV!

Jamie Carragher has apologised for comments he made about Aston Villa and Unai Emery

'I'd like to apologise to Aston Villa, the owners & their fans,' Carragher wrote on social media.

'My language this week was clumsy & wrong. I can assure Villa fans it was tongue in cheek but I can understand it's not come across that way, so apologies. Good luck today UTV!'

Fans were left stunned at the response by Villa to Carragher's comments, seemingly innocuous linking Emery, who is admired at Old Trafford, to the Manchester United job, which may soon be available with immense pressure on Michael Carrick.

‘I think Unai Emery is unbelievable with what he does year after year. That amount of change, players needing time to settle and he does it year after year,' Carragher had said.

'But the reason I’m going to go back at Villa fans is I can’t believe that a manager who is so successful in the Europa League, take a player, if you’d won the Europa League three or four times (Emery has won it five times) surely you’ll then want to go for the Champions League.

‘Aston Villa will never be Manchester United. I just think he didn’t do well at PSG or Arsenal, and maybe that’s because of egos in the dressing room and that sort of thing.

'But surely he would want that opportunity to manage a giant again. There is a chain in football, whether you like it or not.’

#1657. How Amorim engineered a derby masterclass: Tactical analysis of AC Milan 3-1 Inter

AC Milan tasted derby delight for the fourth time in a row as they dismantled Inter in the first half to take the bragging rights.

It did not take long for Milan to go ahead as Christian Pulisic rose highest to nod in a Diego Moreira cross, and just a few minutes later Adrien Rabiot was on hand to finish off a nicely worked set-piece routine to make it 2-0.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Alessandro Bastoni scored from a corner to make it a one-goal game once again, but then Moreira’s free-kick re-established the two-goal lead and that would be enough to see the Rossoneri home after a more controlled secnd half.

It marked a fourth straight win for Milan against the Nerazzurri and it reduces the gap to the city rivals back down to four points. Below is the tactical breakdown from Rohit Rajeev.

Ruben Amorim chose to make six changes from the team that lost to Bologna on Wednesday night, with Mario Gila, Sankhoun Diawara, Luka Modric, Adrien Rabiot, Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic all getting the nod.

Milan started with a 4-4-1-1 formation, with Gila, Moreira and Rabiot returning to the starting XI. However, the structure was far from rigid, frequently shifting between a 4-2-3-1 and a 3-4-2-1. Much of this positional fluidity was dictated by the movements of two players in particular: Diawara and Rabiot.

Milan adopted a 3-4-2-1 structure in possession, using a one-up, one-down mechanism to maintain balance in their build-up.

When both Gila and Diawara pushed forward, Modrić dropped into the defensive line to preserve a back three. This ensured Milan always had three players providing rest defence and protection against counter-attacks.

This was one of the key differences between Amorim and Xabi Alonso’s approach at Chelsea. Alonso was more comfortable leaving just two players at the back, allowing Acheampong to advance and accepting the increased risk of counter-attacks.

Chivu was without his captain and leading goalscorer Lautaro Martínez, while also having one eye on Tuesday’s fixture against Feyenoord. He therefore experimented with a 3-4-2-1 formation, a system that had brought him success during his time at Parma.

Sucic and Diouf operated behind Thuram, with Barella and Çalhanoğlu forming the double pivot. However, the experiment backfired. Inter’s usual 3-5-2 offered greater central presence and allowed them to create numerical overloads, particularly when Lautaro dropped deeper to link play.

Without that additional central presence, Inter struggled to establish the same midfield superiority.

Amorim’s subtle shift from a 3-4-2-1 to a 4-4-1-1 was primarily intended to increase Milan’s presence in the wide areas.

With Inter heavily reliant on the flanks to progress their build-up, Milan used this adjustment to create numerical superiority, often establishing 4v3 situations in wide areas.

This allowed them to outnumber Inter around the ball, restrict their passing options and prevent progression. An effective example of horizontal pressing.

Much has been said about the build-up to Milan’s first goal, particularly the excellent combination play that allowed them to progress from the back and find Moreira. However, what followed was equally important.

A 2v2 situation developed in the wide areas, with Rabiot occupying Bastoni and Moreira taking on Carlos Augusto. Moreira won his individual duel, creating the opportunity to deliver into the box.

While this was unfolding, Milan committed three players into the penalty area: Ramos, Pulisic and Diawara. Pulisic’s movement was particularly intelligent. He initially checked his run, distracting Bisseck, who was more focused on the ball than tracking his opponent.

As the cross arrived, Pulisic moved into the space created by that moment of hesitation, set himself and finished clinically. A goal built on excellent individual quality and intelligent off-ball movement.

A rare set-piece goal for Milan, but one that involved the collective effort of several players. Milan used their players effectively as blockers, almost like in volleyball.

Ramos blocked Sucic, while Pavlovic and De Winter occupied Bisseck and Akanji. Diawara also engaged two Inter players, creating a completely free route between Moreira and Rabiot.

With Inter defending zonally, these blocking movements disrupted their defensive structure and left Rabiot unmarked. On cue, Rabiot attacked the space and met Moreira’s delivery to score.

A well-rehearsed set-piece routine built on intelligent movement and effective blocking.

Milan then moved to a 5-2-3 shape to defend the obvious attack from Inter who looked to recover in the game.

With Milan maintaining a high defensive line, Inter looked to exploit Thuram’s pace by playing chipped through balls into the space behind the defence.

After going 2-0 up, Milan took a significant defensive risk with their approach. The front three of Rabiot, Pulisic and Ramos continued to press high, while the back five held their position.

This created a considerable gap between the two units, which Inter were able to exploit during their counter-attacks.

Inter used rotations in the build-up to create numerical advantages in the wide areas. Barella dropped into the back three, allowing Bisseck to push forward and join Diouf and Spence on the right. This created a 3v2 against Diawara and Pavlovic, with Diawara particularly exposed to a 2v1.

The Nerazzurri replicated the same movement on the opposite flank, with Bastoni advancing and allowing Carlos Augusto to push higher up the pitch. This created the space for Augusto to deliver the cross that led to Djed Spence’s chance.

Inter scored their only goal from a corner. Calhanoglu delivered an inswinging cross, with Akanji making a decoy run towards the near post and flicking the ball on with his head. This movement attracted Milan’s defenders towards the front post, leaving Bastoni unmarked at the far post to head home.

Musah did well to position himself between the ball and Barella, winning a free kick in a dangerous area. Maignan also positioned two Milan players between Inter’s wall and Josep Martinez, obstructing the goalkeeper’s line of sight.

Moreira struck underneath the ball with the upper part of his instep, generating enough lift to send it over the wall and make it 3-1.

With Milan comfortably ahead, Amorim’s priority was to manage the game, and he did so effectively. He dropped the defensive line by around four metres and encouraged Milan to circulate possession more in their own half, avoiding unnecessary risks while Inter were forced to chase the game.

Milan also played more long balls in the second half, reflecting their increased willingness to exploit the spaces left behind by Inter through counter-attacks.

Inter were initially outnumbering Milan in central areas, but Amorim addressed the issue with a tactical adjustment. He instructed Pulisic and Rabiot to drop deeper, forming a midfield triangle that provided additional central support and prevented Inter from creating the same numerical overloads.

Amorim also introduced adjustments to neutralise the wide overloads created by Bisseck and Bastoni. He repositioned Pulisic deeper, asking him to track Bisseck’s movements and prioritise defensive duties over attacking influence. Pulisic therefore operated more like a midfielder than a traditional number 10.

Musah was given a floating role in front of the defence, acting as a screen and covering the spaces left behind whenever Milan’s defenders stepped out to engage an opponent or pushed forward to support an attack.

#1656. Opinion: Liverpool lining up surprise star to replace Alisson Becker

Liverpool are reportedly lining up a surprise move to replace Alisson Becker.

Everything comes to an end. That is the reality of life. It's why life is both beautiful and tragic at the same time. Endings make you appreciate the present, the moments for what they really were - poignant periods of our lives that had a profound impact on us.

Experiences are the greatest tokens we have as humans.

For Liverpool supporters, Alisson brought so many of these profound moments. From incredible saves to standing up in the face of tragedy.

That goal against West Brom. Where he leaped from the sky and thundered the ball into the back of the net with his forehead merely days after losing his father will live long in the memory.

It was during the darkest period of the Covid-19 Pandemic and it brought fans a split-second relief from the doom and gloom.

Alisson's time is coming to an end at LiverpoolWe've seen a lot of legends leave Anfield over the last few years, and Alisson is likely going to be the next one who follows suit. The Brazilian could have left Liverpool last summer, but in the end, the club decided to keep him. He now has less than a year left on his contract with Liverpool, which expires at the end of the season. It's hard to see him being retained any further. He's 34-years-old and he is no longer the incredible goalkeeper that he once was. Liverpool have also very clearly paved the way for his departure. They signed Giorgi Mamardashvili two years ago, brought in Armin Pecsi a year ago and also broke the world record for an U23 goalkeeper when they agreed to sign Lucca Brughmann last summer.

#1655. FC Twente vs Pafos FC - prediction, team news, lineups

By Nsidibe Akpan | 03 Nov 2026 22:18

FC Twente and Pafos FC meet in matchday three of the UEFA Conference League league phase at De Grolsch Veste in Enschede on Thursday and the home team looks to make it three wins from three.

The Tukkers have won both of their matches and sit fifth with six points, while the Paphites are 27th with one point after a 3-1 defeat at Atalanta and a 1-1 home draw with Riga FC.

John van den Brom's side have started their league-phase campaign with a 1-0 home win over Thun and a 4-1 victory at Lincoln Red Imps, their first two successive wins in a major European campaign since 2001-02.

Ramiz Zerrouki scored the only goal against Thun five minutes after the Swiss champions were reduced to 10 men by a debatable red card, and Thomas van den Belt then scored twice in Gibraltar, where Wout Weghorst and Daouda Weidmann also found the net.

The Tukkers followed that by beating AZ 2-0 in Alkmaar on October 25, with Sondre Orjasaeter scoring in the 84th minute and substitute Lucas Vennegoor of Hesselink adding his first Eredivisie goal in stoppage time.

Sunday’s 9-0 win at Excelsior was the biggest in the club’s Eredivisie history, with Weghorst scoring four times for the first time in his career and Orjasaeter becoming the first player to register five assists in an Eredivisie match since the statistic has been recorded.

The scoreline needs context, because Excelsior played 85 minutes with 10 men after Nesto Groen was sent off in the sixth minute for a high challenge on Robin Propper.

The wins at Lincoln, AZ and Excelsior came by a combined 15-1 and followed a 2-1 home defeat by Utrecht on October 18, which remains the Tukkers’ most recent loss in any competition.

Weghorst joined on a free transfer from Ajax in June, reuniting with technical director Erik ten Hag, and after a stuttering start that drew jeers from home supporters he has become the focal point, although a hamstring problem picked up at AZ meant he was taken off after 62 minutes at Excelsior.

Pafos are in the main draw of a European competition for a third consecutive season, having reached the Conference League last 16 in 2024-25 and the Champions League league phase in 2025-26.

This season they beat Hajduk Split 4-2 on aggregate in Europa League qualifying and then lost a third-round tie to Salzburg 4-3 on aggregate, after a 1-0 defeat in Austria and a 3-3 home draw in which they led 2-0 at half-time and conceded three after the break.

They then went through against Dinamo City of Albania 5-3 on aggregate in the Conference League play-off round, drawing 1-1 away and winning 4-2 at home on August 27.

In the league phase, Atalanta led 3-0 at half-time through Elmas, Raspadori and Scamacca on the way to a 3-1 win on October 15, and Biel’s 76th-minute left-footed finish earned a 1-1 draw with Riga FC on October 22 after Caio Ferreira had given the visitors the lead in the 67th minute.

Pafos have conceded in each of their last six European matches, 11 goals in total, a run that includes three against Atalanta and three in the second half of the return leg against Salzburg.

Pafos drew 2-2 at Apollon Limassol on October 31, with Lele giving them the lead after half an hour and substitute Anderson Silva equalising late, which left them winless in four matches in all competitions after the Atalanta defeat and goalless and 1-1 draws with APOEL Nicosia and Riga.

Director Haris Theocharous told Cypriot outlet Goal that the club is not scoring from any area of the pitch and wants a restart, although he said head coach Ricardo Sa Pinto’s position is not under pressure.

Sa Pinto, who succeeded Albert Celades, leads a squad that finished fourth in the Cypriot First Division last season on 62 points and won the Cypriot Cup, with Anderson Silva scoring 14 goals in all competitions and Joao Correia 10 in the league.

Twente are without goalkeeper Lars Unnerstall, defenders Max Bruns and Stav Lemkin, and winger Filip Thorvaldsen, who has a knee injury, and none of the four is expected back before the international break.

Ruud Nijstad and Propper have formed the centre-back pairing in the absence of Bruns and Lemkin, with 18-year-old Jip Meilink making his debut at Lincoln, while Joel Drommel has kept goal in the league phase.

Weidmann served his Eredivisie suspension at Excelsior after a second yellow card at AZ and is expected to be available again, although Van den Belt, who has three goals across the Lincoln and Excelsior games, has done enough to keep his place.

Weghorst and Orjasaeter were both taken off after roughly an hour at Excelsior as part of a plan agreed at half-time, and with Ajax visiting Enschede on Sunday, Van den Brom may manage their minutes again.

Pafos have a long injury list, with goalkeeper Jay Gorter and forward Jaja out long term, David Goldar, Nicolas Ngamaleu and Pepe among those who have missed recent weeks, and Jonatas Noro ruled out in late October.

David Luiz and Biel were reported to have fitness complaints last weekend, but Luiz returned to the starting lineup at Apollon Limassol and Radoslaw Majecki has kept goal in Gorter’s absence, so Sa Pinto is expected to start from the lineup that faced Riga.

Silva came off the bench at Apollon Limassol after starting against Riga, which suggests Sa Pinto may rotate his attack again, with Lele pushing for a place after his goal.

Drommel; Van Rooij, Propper, Nijstad, Adelgaard; Zerrouki, Taha, Van den Belt; Rots, Orjasaeter, Weghorst

Majecki; Bruno, Mmaee, Luiz, Ioannou; Guga, Dragomir, Brito; Correia, Biel, Anderson Silva

Pafos have conceded in each of their last six European matches, including falling 3-0 behind at half-time against Atalanta and surrendering a 2-0 lead against Salzburg, which represents a worrying defensive record ahead of facing a Twente side that have scored 15 goals across their last three away matches.

However, Twente benefited from playing against 10 men for long spells in their matches against Thun and Excelsior, while they are also without four injured players, and with Pafos scoring in five of their last six European fixtures, the hosts are backed to find the net, although a heavy defeat remains difficult to rule out.

#1654. ‘He looks like Rudiger’ - former coach on Real Madrid youngster Lamini Fati

By Alexis Pereira | 03 Nov 2026 22:25, Last updated: 03 Nov 2026 23:00

Real Madrid already have a ‘mini-Rudiger’ in Castilla defender Lamini Fati, according to his former coach. Manolo Rueda, who managed the 20-year-old in Leganes’ Under-19s, has told AS that he sees a future Real Madrid first-team centre-back.

Fati is a jewel of La Fabrica. The Spain youth centre-back joined the academy in the summer of 2025 from Leganes and has already made his first appearances for the senior team under boss Jose Mourinho in pre-season.

After starting the season on the bench, Fati has played the last three Castilla games and made his first start against Algeciras (2-0) on 25 October. He was already mentioned in March as a possible solution to a defensive injury crisis, but he appears to need to establish himself in the reserves before hoping to join Mourinho’s squad.

Rueda explained Fati’s characteristics. ‘The quality that stands out most is the security and power he brings to the game. And a characteristic that I think is very underrated is his heading. I think he is very, very, very good in the air in attack. He scores goals and, defensively, he is very forceful.’

To break into Real Madrid’s defensive rotation, Fati has some points to improve. ‘I think Lamini has to bring continuity and speed in actions with the ball,’ Rueda said. ‘Without the ball, he has everything he needs. He has to refine some technical and tactical aspects, but he will get there with age, games and accumulated minutes.’

The 46-year-old sees a bright future. ‘Real Madrid currently have two excellent centre-backs in their squad, Konate and Rudiger. He looks a lot like them and could pair up with either. That is why I think he has a genuine chance of becoming a starting defender at Real Madrid.’

Fati may not get the chance to partner Rudiger, whose contract runs out at the end of the season, aged 33, but he could potentially replace him. ‘He is a player who looks like Rudiger,’ Rueda said. ‘He is aggressive in duels and simplifies actions with the ball. Both have very clear ideas and can execute their tasks at a very high level. Lamini needs to reach that level. If he can reproduce those efforts and behaviours at excellence, we could see “a mini-Rudiger”.’

#1653. GdS: Amorim ‘changes the pieces’ – his plan to rotate vs. Ferencvaros in must-win game

AC Milan don’t have much time to enjoy their derby win over Inter, as a key European game awaits on Thursday night.

La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) begin a report this morning by writing that this week marks the beginning of a genuine push toward success in the Europa League. The momentum gained from the derby victory must be harnessed and used properly.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

For a Milan side capable of dismantling Chivu’s team with three goals in 45 minutes, the Ferencváros game should pose no real concern. It must, however, be approached with focus and a significant yet carefully considered rotation of the squad.

The situation mirrors the league campaign in one key respect: the table. By winning on Saturday, Milan got back into the hunt for the Scudetto, so a similar result is needed in Europe. The Rossoneri currently sit on three points, while the Hungarians have a perfect record of nine.

Even with a win, Milan won’t catch their opponents, but they will improve their position in the table which is a necessity, especially with only four games left after this.

Ferencvaros’ position in the standings is the result of a long, arduous journey. They began their Europa League campaign in the first qualifying round, eliminating Serbia’s Vojvodina.

In the second round, they knocked out the Dutch side Twente. They then triumphed over Poland’s Górnik Zabrze in the third round, before defeating Trabzonspor in the play-offs.

All that hard work has paid off in the league phase, where they have secured three wins out of three – against Celtic, Plzeň and Torreense – making them one of only five teams with a perfect record. The others are Benfica, Leverkusen, Bournemouth and Olympiacos.

Two of these four have already faced the Rossoneri, which speaks to the challenging nature of Milan’s schedule. Against the Portuguese side, Amorim faltered in his debut, fielding a side packed with reserves in a high-profile match.

Against Bournemouth, the result was compromised by two penalties and Mike Maignan’s red card. In between, there was a resounding victory in Salzburg, spearheaded by Alphadjo Cissé. This explains why they currently sit on just three points, a situation that now demands a turnaround.

The upcoming schedule is relatively more manageable, featuring an away trip to Athens, a home match against Sunderland, a visit to Sofia to face Levski, and a game against Ararat Armenia in Milan.

Securing a spot in the round of 16 is a task that needs to be completed, and preferably soon. Sitting on three points in 24th place, Milan’s current standing in the Europa League does not reflect the goal the club have set for themselves: to go all the way in the competition.

Cisse will return to the starting line-up for the competition in which he is the team’s top scorer: three goals, all netted on the same night in Austria. The squad will once again be adjusted to accommodate the turnover and rotations necessary for managing resources.

This time, the team are better prepared to absorb these changes after welcoming back some players before the derby. Consequently, there will be further rotation on Thursday night, with the aim of keeping everyone fresh.

A change is unavoidable in goal, where the suspension for the captain Maignan will see Lorenzo Torriani make his first start. In defence, Sankhoun Diawara could play centrally, while Pervis Estupinan or Davide Bartesaghi (or both, with the latter pushed further forward) could feature on the left.

In midfield, Ardon Jashari will take on a Modrić-like role, while the versatile Filippo Terracciano could slot in as a mezzala (or even at right-back, covering for Mario Gila). There is also a chance of seeing the very young Christian Comotto in action.

In attack, Omari Hutchinson is a certain starter:he looked lively during his time on the pitch against Bologna and performed even better against Udinese, a match in which he scored his first goal for Milan. Cisse could lead the line, but Francesco Camarda and Goncalo Ramos remain candidates too.

#1652. Barcelona eye Arsenal’s Hincapie as January centre-back option

By Alexis Pereira | 03 Nov 2026 22:37

Barcelona, also recently linked with Paris SG Willian Pacho, have contacted the representatives of Arsenal defender Piero Hincapie as they plan to sign a centre-back in the January transfer window, with boss Hansi Flick said to approve of the Ecuadorian’s profile.

Barcelona are already looking ahead to the winter market, which opens in a little under two months. A first shortlist of four names has been revealed, featuring Alessandro Bastoni, Josko Gvardiol, Natan and Lisandro Martinez, but Actualite Barca, relayed by Sport, says Hincapie is also a target.

Hincapie signed permanently for Arsenal last summer for £34m, after a season on loan with the Gunners. Despite that and the absence of William Saliba since the start of the campaign, the 24-year-old has played little, making seven appearances with only two starts.

His profile still matches what Barcelona want. Flick likes his versatility between centre-back and left-back, a quality that could prove useful if Alejandro Balde leaves in January, as expected.

Sporting director Deco has already established first contact with the player’s entourage, aiming to gauge his willingness to move and explore a winter exit.

The deal will not be simple, however. Boss Mikel Arteta does not view Hincapie, who came from Bayer Leverkusen in 2024, as a regular starter, but he values the player and will be reluctant to let him leave mid-season. Arsenal will also not want to take a loss on the transfer, so they would ask for at least £34m, a significant sum for Barcelona’s finances.

#1651. Sean Dyche emerges as ‘leading contender’ as Crystal Palace consider Pierre Sage’s future

Barnaby Lane is a highly experienced sports writer who has written for The Times, FourFourTwo Magazine, Sports Illustrated, TalkSPORT, and Business Insider. Over the years, he's had the pleasure of interviewing some of the biggest names in world sport, including Usain Bolt, Rafael Nadal, Christian Pulisic, and more.

Crystal Palace are reportedly considering their managerial options after a difficult start to the Premier League season, with former Nottingham Forest boss Sean Dyche emerging as a potential replacement for Pierre Sage.

The Eagles’ disappointing results have increased pressure on Sage, whose side suffered a 2-0 defeat to Newcastle United on Sunday.

With Palace struggling near the relegation zone, the club could face an important decision over whether to persist with their current manager.

According to The Telegraph, Dyche is among the leading candidates should Palace decide to part ways with Sage.

The 55-year-old has been without a managerial position since leaving Nottingham Forest in February. His experience in Premier League survival battles could appeal to Palace as they attempt to turn their season around.

Dyche previously established his reputation at Burnley, guiding the club into the Premier League and keeping them in the top flight for several seasons. He also helped Everton avoid relegation during his time at Goodison Park.

Other names have reportedly entered the conversation, including Thomas Frank and Vítor Pereira, although Palace have not officially announced a change of manager.

Sage arrived at Selhurst Park with expectations following his successful spell at Lens, but results in England have proved challenging.

The defeat against Newcastle followed a heavy loss to Brighton, leaving Palace with just two Premier League victories from their opening eight matches. Their defensive problems have been particularly concerning, with 19 goals conceded.

Despite the speculation, Sage has maintained that he believes the players and club hierarchy remain behind him. His immediate challenge is to improve results and ease fears of a relegation battle.

What this means for Crystal Palace: Dyche’s experience makes him a reported option if Palace decide to change direction. However, no appointment has been confirmed, and Sage’s future remains dependent on the club’s next decision.

#1650. Lisandro Martinez's self-destruction sums up a broken Man United as Michael Carrick's future hangs by a thread - and there are still questions to ask of Xabi Alonso's Chelsea, writes IAN HERBERT

Published: 10:52 EDT, 31 October 2026 | Updated: 12:01 EDT, 31 October 2026

The sun was high and fierce and Michael Carrick shielded his eyes from it on the few occasions he got to his feet and tried to direct the Manchester United players, who did not seem to hear him. The United contingent hurled personal abuse at Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Jason Wilcox. The scrutiny was remorseless and unyielding.

For a time, there seemed to be hope - and no one can say that this latest hammer blow for Carrick removes the doubts about Xabi Alonso’s methods – but it was crushed by the same fecklessness and mindlessness that is burying United alive.

Carrick did not cast so much as a glance at Lisandro Martinez - who had just finished off the team’s hopes by leaping with Wesley Fofana and extending an elbow into his face to concede a penalty - when he walked past on the way to the tunnel.

Bruno Fernandes and some others made a half-hearted protest about the dismissal but Carrick didn’t. He knew. This looked for all the world like a footballer looking to leave the field early – making no attempt to play the ball as he was up with Fofana, having been booked for a reckless challenge on Morgan Rogers, just three minutes earlier.

The Argentinian, whose words publicly challenging the club a few weeks back will always belong to the story of these Carrick-era death throes, will perhaps want to trash talk the club again when he has been shown the door. But it was also his own gross inadequacy which had allowed Morgan Rogers to dance through the defence to put Chelsea ahead. Martinez should never darken the door of a United squad again.

Michael Carrick’s future at Manchester United looks increasingly untenable after his side imploded in the second half to lose 2-0 against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge

Lisandro Martinez, publicly outspoken earlier this month, was booked twice inside two minutes

There are few grounds for optimism from here but Fernandes is one. When he forfeited the chance to write a new script for himself – blasting into the stand after Bryan Mbeumo’s cross had gifted him a golden opportunity – the prospect of him righting the wrongs of the past week seemed forlorn.

By then, he had already been dumped on his backside by Romeo Lavia and Moises Caicedo and ceded possession. But he brushed off the mockery of the Chelsea faithful to put in a performance which demonstrated that he has a part to play at United.

In front of the small United away section before the game, he went through a free-kick taking routine, arcing one into the top-left corner and striking another against the bar.

He was the one who saw the picture late in the first half, sliding in a pass which sent Amad in. When United went 2-0 down, he conferred with Carrick. He lingered before United’s fans at the end and they accepted him. The turmoil remains but he will be needed.

Fernandes was the one who saw the picture late in the first half, sliding in a pass which sent Amad in and United went 2-0 down, he conferred with Carrick

There can be no overstating the gravity of the week just passed for Xabi Alonso: a lamentable performance in defeat to Tottenham, the Carabao Cup defeat to Liverpool and the Spaniard’s suggestion that trophy didn’t matter, which has gone down badly with the fans.

His brief programme notes made it clear how much he wanted something better here but the yawning gaps between Chelsea’s midfield and defensive lines and the ease with which United exploited them in the first half were disturbing. Wesley Fofana was lamentable.

United’s Amad could have plundered them twice – first burgling Fofana on the half-way line but lacking the pace to accelerate on and score, then easing into space and failing to despatch when one-on-one with Mike Penders. Cole Palmer’s error allowed Matheus Cunha to send Fernandes off but Mbeumo couldn’t connect with his cross. United’s failure to capitalise was fateful.

Wesley Fofana was lamentable and United’s Amad Diallo could have plundered them twice

As both sides squandered chances and laboured under basic defensive challenges, it was hard to countenance the notion that two gladiators of European football used to compete in this fixture and actually contested a Champions League final.

The occasion cried out for a moment of class and it was Morgan Rogers who provided it, taking a ball Romeo Lavia had won, dancing his way through half of the Manchester United team and slipping the ball home.

The defending shamed the traditions of the visiting team. Carlos Baleba, Andrey Santos, Martinez and Harry Maguire just watched Morgan go. But it was Rogers, taking his Chelsea tally to six goals and four assists in all competitions, who turned the game around.

Morgan Rogers had scored a brilliant solo goal for Chelsea's second-half opener to show up United’s awful finishing

It was always clear that the test of United’s mettle would come if they fell behind. The general view of the fans marching through Euston Station at 11am was that if United scored first they would come away with the points. If they conceded, their heads would drop and the psychological failure at the heart of this team would come to the fore. And so it came to pass.

In a straw poll of 15 or so at Euston, only two thought Carrick was the man to restore ‘Standards’, to quote the mantra captured on an Old Trafford banner last week. The way Chelsea turned the screw just bore that pessimism. Cole Palmer converted the penalty Martinez had conceded to finish things off.

It was to the jubilant cheers of the Chelsea faithful that Estevao left the field towards the end and this was an afternoon which will live long in the memory for him. Twice he had the ball in United’s net – pouncing on Senne Lammens' failure to hold a cross in the first half and taking Palmer’s pass to crash home in the second – but twice he was denied by VAR.

By the end, he had the control of Chelsea’s right as he interlinked with Palmer and came close a third time. Some will say this calls into question Alonso’s decision to limit his game time so far, though it was only as United fell away to nothing that he ran the show.

Some will say Estevao's display calls into question Alonso’s decision to limit his game time so far, though it was only as United fell away to nothing that he ran the show

As the minutes ticked down on another desperate result for United, the away section sang Carrick’s name once more and, significantly, he walked over towards them alone once more, just as he had after the defeat at home to Bournemouth. But it was a less emphatic assertion of empathy and support for him this time, and he did not linger so long.

The talk of Eddie Howe’s availability grows. It emerged on Saturday that under the terms of his departure agreement with Newcastle United that he will cost United only £3million. The United fans are really not convinced by him and it looks like the club will work through many more managers before a corner is turned. The constant will be that support base, who began and ended the match singing Sir Matt Busby’s name. They will always have their history.

Paris Saint-Germain are reportedly keen on Celta Vigo defender Javi Rodriguez, with Luis Enrique an admirer of the Spaniard’s profile. The 23-year-old is also attracting interest from four Premier League clubs.

#1647. CM: Cardinale prepares ‘aggressive’ mercato – the targets for each department

Gerry Cardinale has declared that AC Milan will be active in the winter mercato, but who is on the potential shopping list?

Calciomercato.com write that Milan are constantly evolving, with owner Gerry Cardinale fully immersed in the club’s dynamics, aiming to create a winning team. The foundations have been laid with the signings of Mario Gila, Diego Moreira and Goncalo Ramos from the summer.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Then came the renewals of two key players, Strahinja Pavlovic and Christian Pulisic. Official announcements regarding the contract extensions of Adrien Rabiot and Alphadjo Cisse, two of the players who have had a devastating impact this start to the season.

However, Cardinale spoke to La Gazzetta dello Sport and revealed a desire to do more: “We need to continue improving the squad because I wasn’t able to do everything I wanted in the summer. It will probably take a couple more transfer windows to complete everything.

“We’re only a quarter of the way there, and the priority is building a team that can deal with injuries. That’s why we’ll continue to be aggressive in the January transfer market. I won’t waste money, but when I set my mind on signing a player, I do everything I can to achieve it.”

There’s no doubt about one thing: Milan will sign a defender in January. Maybe two. The hottest name – Ruben Amorim’s favourite – is Goncalo Inacio from Sporting CP, with whom discussions began last summer.

Also on the list is Kim Min-Jae at Bayern Munich, with direct contact having been established in recent days. Looking to the future, Borussia Dortmund’s Luca Reggiani and Manchester United’s Leny Yoro are being eyed.

A potential right-back signing is also being considered: Argentine international Agustin Giay is among those being monitored . The 22-year-old from Palmeiras is worth around €13m.

In midfield, Pierre-Emile Højbjerg remains a real possibility for January if Milan decides to sign a central midfielder in the January transfer window. In that case, Christian Comotto would be loaned out: Parma, Monza, and half of Serie B are following him.

Sassuolo’s Darryl Bakola is highly sought after, while Bournemouth’s Alex Scott is the dream for next season. Two players Milan are following are the Swede Yasin Ayari and the Paraguayan Diego Gomez of Brighton. Cagliari’s Alessandro Romano is also highly sought after.

The idea is to make a five-star signing for the attack, and Cardinale’s obsession is Real Madrid’s Endrick. Nicolo Tresoldi is liked, but the problem remains Club Brugge who are tough negotiators. For the future, the focus is on Cagliari’s Paul Mendy and Monza’s Gustavo Varela.
